1.1: The wordes of Jeremiah the sonne of Hilkiah one of the Priests that were at Anathoth in the land of Beniamin.
1.2: To whom the word of the Lord came in the dayes of Josiah the sonne of Amon King of Judah in the thirteenth yeere of his reign:
1.3: And also in the dayes of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah unto the end of the eleventh yeere of Zedekiah, the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, even unto the carying away of Jerusalem captive in the fift moneth.
1.4: Then the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
1.5: Before I formed thee in the womb, I knew thee, and before thou camest out of the womb, I sanctified thee, and ordeined thee to be a Prophet unto the nations.
1.6: Then said I, Oh, Lord God, behold, I can not speak, for I am a child.
1.7: But the Lord said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt goe to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee, shalt thou speak.
1.8: Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord.
1.9: Then the Lord stretched out his hand and touched my mouth, and the Lord said unto me, Behold, I have put my wordes in thy mouth.
1.10: Behold, this day have I set thee over the nations and over the kingdomes to pluck up, and to root out, and to destroy and throw down, to build, and to plant.
1.11: After this the word of the Lord came unto me, saying, Jeremiah, what seest thou? And I said, I see a rod of an almond tree.
1.12: Then said the Lord unto me, Thou hast seen aright: for I will hasten my word to perform it.
1.13: Again the word of the Lord came unto me the second time, saying, What seest thou? And I said, I see a seething pot looking out of the North.
1.14: Then said the Lord unto me, Out of the North shall a plague be spred upon all the inhabitants of the land.
1.15: For loe, I will call all the families of the kingdomes of the North, saith the Lord, and they shall come, and every one shall set his throne in the entring of the gates of Jerusalem, and on all the walles thereof round about, and in all the cities of Judah.
1.16: And I will declare unto them my iudgements touching all the wickedness of them that have forsaken me, and have burnt incense unto other gods, and worshipped the workes of their own handes.
1.17: Thou therefore trusse up thy loynes, and arise and speak unto them all that I commaund thee: be not afraid of their faces, lest I destroy thee before them.
1.18: For I, behold, I this day have made thee a defenced citie, and an yron pillar and walles of brass against the whole land, against the Kings of Judah, and against the princes thereof, against the Priestes thereof and against the people of the land.
1.19: For they shall fight against thee, but they shall not prevail against thee: for I am with thee to deliver thee, sayth the Lord.

2.1: Moreover, the woorde of the Lord came unto me, saying,
2.2: Goe, and crie in the eares of Jerusalem, saying, Thus sayeth the Lord, I remember thee, with the kindenes of thy youth and the love of thy marriage, when thou wentest after me in the wildernes in a land that was not sowen.
2.3: Israel was as a thing halowed unto the Lord, and his first fruits: all they that eat it, shall offend: evil shall come upon them, saith the Lord.
2.4: Hear ye the word of the Lord, O house of Iaakob, and all the families of the house of Israel.
2.5: Thus sayeth the Lord, What iniquitie have your fathers found in mee, that they are gone far from mee, and have walked after vanitie, and are become vain?
2.6: For they said not, Where is the Lord that brought us up out of the land of Egypt? that led us through the wilderness, through a desert, and waste land, through a drie land, and by the shadow of death, by a land that no man passed through, and where no man dwelt?
2.7: And I brought you into a plentiful countrey, to eat the fruit thereof, and the commodities of the same: but when yee entred, yee defiled my land, and made mine heritage an abomination.
2.8: The priests said not, Where is the Lord? and they that should minister the Law, knew me not: the pastours also offended against me, and the Prophets prophesied in Baal, and went after things that did not profit.
2.9: Wherefore I wil yet plead with you, saith the Lord, and I will plead with your childrens children.
2.10: For goe ye to the yles of Chittim, and behold, and send unto Kedar. and take diligent heed, and see whether there be such things.
2.11: Hath any nation changed their gods, which yet are no gods? but my people have chaged their glorie, for that which doeth not profit.
2.12: O yee heavens, be astonied at this: bee afraid and utterly confounded, sayeth the Lord.
2.13: For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken mee the fountain of living waters, to digge them pittes, even broken pittes, that can hold no water.
2.14: Is Israel a seruaunt, or is hee borne in the house? why then is he spoiled?
2.15: The lions roared upon him and yelled, and they have made his land waste: his cities are burnt without an inhabitant.
2.16: Also the children of Noph and Tahapanes have broken thine head.
2.17: Hast not thou procured this unto thy self, because thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, when he led thee by the way?
2.18: And what hast thou now to do in the way of Egypt? to drink the water of Nilus? or what makest thou in the way of Asshur? to drink the water of the River?
2.19: Thine own wickednes shall correct thee, and thy turnings back shall reprooue thee: know therefore and behold, that it is an evil thing, and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, sayeth the Lord God of hostes.
2.20: For of old time I have broken thy yoke, and burst thy bondes, and thou saidest, I will no more transgress, but like an harlot thou runnest about upon al hie hilles, and under all green trees.
2.21: Yet I had planted thee, a noble vine, whose plants were all natural: how then art thou turned unto me into the plants of a strange vine?
2.22: Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much sop, yet thine iniquitie is marked before me, sayeth the Lord God.
2.23: How canst thou say, I am not polluted, neither have I followed Baalim? behold thy waies in the valley, and know, what thou hast done: thou art like a swift dromedarie, that runneth by his waies.
2.24: And as a wild ass, used to the wilderness, that snuffeth up the wind by occasion at her pleasure: who can turn her back? all they that seek her, will not wearie themselves, but wil find her in her moneth.
2.25: Keep thou thy feet from barenes, and thy throte from thirst: but thou saidest desperately, No, for I have loved strangers, and them will I follow.
2.26: As the theefe is ashamed, when he is foud, so is the house of Israel ashamed, they, their kings, their princes and their Priests, and their Prophets,
2.27: Saying to a tree, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast begotten me: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in ye time of their troble they wil say, Arise, and help us.
2.28: But where are thy gods, that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can help thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the nomber of thy cities, are thy gods, O Judah.
2.29: Wherefore wil ye plead with me? ye all have rebelled against me, sayeth the Lord.
2.30: I have smitten your children in vain, they received no correction: your own sword hath deuoured your Prophets like a destroying lyon.
2.31: O generation, take heed to the word of the Lord: have I been as a wilderness unto Israel? or a land of darkenesse? Wherefore sayeth my people then, We are lordes, we will come no more unto thee?
2.32: Can a maid forget her ornament, or a bride her attire? yet my people have forgotten me, daies without number.
2.33: Why doest thou prepare thy way, to seek amitie? even therefore will I teach thee, that thy waies are wickedness.
2.34: Also in thy wings is found the bloud of the soules of ye poor innocents: I have not found it in holes, but upon all these places.
2.35: Yet thou saiest, Because I am giltles, surely his wrath shall turn from mee: behold, I will enter with thee into iudgement, because thou saiest, I have not sinned.
2.36: Why runnest thou about so much to change thy waies? for thou shalt be confounded of Egypt, as thou art confounded of Asshur.
2.37: For thou shalt goe foorth from thence, and thine hands upon thine head, because the Lord hath reiected thy confidence, and thou shalt not prosper thereby.

3.1: They say, If a man put away his wife, and she goe from him, and become another mans, shall hee return again unto her? shall not this land be polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers: yet turn again to mee, sayeth the Lord.
3.2: Lift up thine eyes unto the hie places, and behold, where thou hast not plaied the harlot: thou hast sit waiting for them in the waies, as the Arabian in the wilderness: and thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredomes, and with thy malice.
3.3: Therefore the showres have been restrained, and the latter rain came not, and thou haddest a whores forehead: thou wouldest not bee ashamed.
3.4: Diddest thou not stil crie unto me, Thou art my father, and the guide of my youth?
3.5: Wil he keep his anger for ever? will he reserve it to the end? thus hast thou spoken, but thou doest evil, even more and more.
3.6: The Lord said also unto me, in the daies of Josiah the King, Hast thou seen what this rebel Israel hath done? for she hath gone up upon every high mountain, and under every green tree, and there plaied the harlot.
3.7: And I sayde, when she had done all this, Turn thou unto me: but she returned not, as her rebellious sister Judah saw.
3.8: When I saw, how that by all occasions rebellious Israel had plaied the harlot, I cast her away, and gave her a bill of divorcement: yet her rebellious sister Judah was not afraied, but she went also, and plaied the harlot.
3.9: So that for the lightness of her whoredom she hath even defiled the land: for she hath committed fornication with stones and stockes.
3.10: Nevertheless for all this, her rebellious sister Judah hath not returned unto mee with her whole heart, but fainedly, sayth the Lord.
3.11: And the Lord said unto me, The rebellious Israel hath justified her self more then the rebellious Judah.
3.12: Goe and crie these woordes toward the North and say, Thou disobedient Israel, return, sayeth the Lord, and I will not let my wrath fall upon you: for I am merciful, sayeth the Lord, and I will not alway keep mine anger.
3.13: But know thine iniquitie: for thou hast rebelled against the Lord thy God, and hast scattered thy waies to the straunge gods under every green tree, but yee would not obey my voyce, sayeth the Lord.
3.14: O yee disobedient children, turn again, sayeth the Lord, for I am your Lord, and I will take you one of a citie, and two of a tribe and wil bring you to Zion,
3.15: And I will give you pastours according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.
3.16: Moreover, when yee be increased and multiplied in the land, in those daies, saieth the Lord, they shall say no more, The Ark of the covenant of the Lord: for it shall come no more to mind, neither shall they remember it, neither shall they visit it, for that shalbe no more done.
3.17: At that time they shall cal Jerusalem, The throne of the Lord, and all the nations shall be gathered unto it, even to the Name of the Lord in Jerusalem: and thence foorth they shall follow no more the hardness of their wicked heart.
3.18: In those daies ye house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the North, into the land, that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.
3.19: But I sayde, How did I take thee for children and give thee a pleasant land, even the glorious heritage of the armies of the heathen, and said, Thou shalt call mee, saying, My father, and shalt not turn from me?
3.20: But as a woman rebelleth against her husband: so have yee rebelled against me, O house of Israel, sayeth the Lord.
3.21: A voice was heard upon the hie places, weeping and supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted their way, and forgotten the Lord their God.
3.22: O yee disobedient children, return and I wil heal your rebellions. Behold, we come unto thee, for thou art the Lord our God.
3.23: Truely the hope of the hilles is but vain, nor the multitude of mountaines: but in the Lord our God is the health of Israel.
3.24: For confusion hath deuoured our fathers labour, from our youth their sheep and their bullocks, their sonnes and their daughters.
3.25: Wee lie down in our confusion, and our shame covereth us: for we have sinned against the Lord our God, we and our fathers from our youth, even unto this day, and have not obeyed the voyce of the Lord our God.

4.1: O Israel, if thou return, return unto me, saith the Lord: and if thou put away thine abominations out of my sight, then shalt thou not remove.
4.2: And thou shalt swear, The Lord liveth in trueth, in iudgement, and in righteousness, and the nations shall be blessed in him, and shall glorie in him.
4.3: For thus saith the Lord to the men of Judah, and to Jerusalem,
4.4: Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among the thornes: be circumcised to the Lord, and take away the foreskinnes of your hearts, ye men of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my wrath come foorth like fire, and burn, that none can quench it, because of the wickedness of your inventions.
4.5: Declare in Judah, and shew forth in Jerusalem, and say, Blow the trumpet in the land: cry, and gather together, and say, Assemble your selves, and let us goe into strong cities.
4.6: Set up the standart in Zion: prepare to flee, and stay not: for I will bring a plague from the North, and a great destruction.
4.7: The lyon is come up from his denne, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is departed, and gone forth of his place to lay thy land waste, and thy cities shalbe destroyed without an inhabitant.
4.8: Wherefore gird you with sackecloth: lament, and howl, for the fierce wrath of the Lord is not turned back from us.
4.9: And in that day, saith the Lord, the heart of the King shall perish, and the heart of the princes and the Priestes shall be astonished, and the Prophets shall wonder.
4.10: Then said I, Ah, Lord God, surely thou hast deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, Ye shall have peace, and the sword perceth unto the heart.
4.11: At that time shall it bee said to this people and to Jerusalem, A dry wind in the hie places of the wildernes cometh toward ye daughter of my people, but neither to fanne nor to clense.
4.12: A mightie wind shall come unto me from those places, and now will I also give sentence upon them.
4.13: Behold, he shall come up as the cloudes, and his charets shalbe as a tempest: his horses are lighter then eagles. Woe unto us, for wee are destroyed.
4.14: O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickednes, that thou maiest be saved: how long shall thy wicked thoughtes remain within thee?
4.15: For a voyce declareth from Dan, and publisheth affliction from mount Ephraim.
4.16: Make ye mention of the heathen, and publish in Jerusalem, Behold, the skoutes come from a far countrey, and crie out against the cities of Judah.
4.17: They have compassed her about as the watchmen of the field, because it hath provoked me to wrath, saith the Lord.
4.18: Thy wayes and thine inventions have procured thee these things, such is thy wickedness: therefore it shall be bitter, therefore it shall perce unto thine heart.
4.19: My bely, my bely, I am pained, even at the very heart: mine heart is troubled within me: I cannot be still: for my soul hath heard the sound of the trumpet, and the alarm of the battell.
4.20: Destruction upon destruction is cryed, for the whole land is wasted: suddenly are my tents destroyed, and my curtaines in a moment.
4.21: How long shall I see the standert, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
4.22: For my people is foolish, they have not knowen me: they are foolish children, and have none understanding: they are wise to doe evil, but to doe well they have no knowledge.
4.23: I have looked upon the earth, and loe, it was without form and void: and to the heavens, and they had no light.
4.24: I beheld the mountaines: and loe, they trembled and all the hilles shook.
4.25: I beheld, and loe, there was no man, and all the birdes of the heaven were departed.
4.26: I beheld, and loe, the fruitful place was a wilderness, and all the cities thereof were broken down at the presence of the Lord, and by his fierce wrath.
4.27: For thus hath the Lord said, The whole land shall be desolate: yet will I not make a full end.
4.28: Therefore shall the earth mourn, and the heavens above shall be darkened, because I have pronounced it: I have thought it, and will not repent, neither will I turn back from it.
4.29: The whole citie shall flee, for the noyse of the horsemen and bowemen: they shall goe into thickets, and clime up upon the rockes: every citie shall be forsaken, and not a man dwell therein.
4.30: And when thou shalt be destroyed, what wilt thou doe? Though thou clothest thy self with skarlet, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou paintest thy face with colours, yet shalt thou trimme thy self in vain: for thy lovers will abhorre thee and seek thy life.
4.31: For I have heard a noyse as of a woman travailing, or as one labouring of her first child, even the voyce of the daughter Zion that sigheth and stretcheth out her handes: woe is me now: for my soul fainteth because of the murtherers.

5.1: Run to and from by the streetes of Jerusalem, and behold now, and know, and inquire in the open places thereof, if ye can find a man, or if there be any that executeth iudgement, and seeketh the trueth, and I will spare it.
5.2: For though they say, The Lord liveth, yet doe they swear falsely.
5.3: O Lord, are not thine eyes upon the trueth? thou hast striken them, but they have not sorowed: thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder then a stone, and have refused to return.
5.4: Therefore I said, Surely they are poor, they are foolish, for they know not the way of the Lord, nor the iudgement of their God.
5.5: I will get me unto the great men, and will speak unto them: for they have knowen the way of the Lord, and the iudgement of their God: but these have altogether broken the yoke, and burst the bondes.
5.6: Wherefore a lyon out of the forest shall slay them, and a wolf of the wilderness shall destroy them: a leopard shall watch over their cities: every one that goeth out thence, shall be torn in pieces, because their trespasses are many, and their rebellions are increased.
5.7: How should I spare thee for this? thy children have forsaken me, and sworn by them that are no gods: though I fed them to the full, yet they committed adulterie, and assembled them selves by companies in the harlots houses.
5.8: They rose up in the morning like fed horses: for every man neyed after his neighbours wife.
5.9: Shall I not visit for these things, saith the Lord? Shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
5.10: Clime up upon their walles, and destroy them, but make not a full end: take away their batilments, for they are not the Lords.
5.11: For the house of Israel, and the house of Judah have grieuously trespassed against me, saith the Lord.
5.12: They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he, neither shall the plague come upon us, neither shall we see sword nor famine.
5.13: And the Prophetes shall be as wind, and the word is not in them: thus shall it come unto them.
5.14: Wherefore thus saith the Lord God of hostes, Because ye speak such wordes, behold, I will put my wordes into thy mouth, like a fire, and this people shall be as wood, and it shall deuoure them.
5.15: Loe, I will bring a nation upon you from far, O house of Israel, saith the Lord, which is a mightie nation, and an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say.
5.16: Whose quiuer is as an open sepulchre: they are all very strong.
5.17: And they shall eat thine harvest and thy bread: they shall deuoure thy sonnes and thy daughters: they shall eat up thy sheep and thy bullocks: they shall eat thy vines and thy figge trees: they shall destroy with the sword thy fenced cities, wherein thou didest trust.
5.18: Nevertheless at those dayes, sayth the Lord, I will not make a full end of you.
5.19: And when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God doe these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.
5.20: Declare this in the house of Iaakob, and publish it in Judah, saying,
5.21: Hear now this, O foolish people, and without understanding, which have eyes and see not, which have eares and hear not.
5.22: Fear ye not me, saith the Lord? or will ye not be afraid at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bounds of the sea by the perpetual decree that it cannot pass it, and though the waves thereof rage, yet can they not prevail, though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?
5.23: But this people hath an unfaithful and rebellious heart: they are departed and gone.
5.24: For they say not in their heart, Let us now fear the Lord our God, that giveth rain both early and late in due season: hee reserveth unto us the appointed weekes of the harvest.
5.25: Yet your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sinnes have hindred good things from you.
5.26: For among my people are found wicked persons, that lay wait as hee that setteth snares: they have made a pit, to catch men.
5.27: As a cage is full of birdes, so are their houses full of deceit: thereby they are become great and waxen rich.
5.28: They are waxen fat and shining: they doe overpass the deedes of the wicked: they execute no iudgement, no not the iudgement of the fatherless: yet they prosper, though they execute no iudgement for the poor.
5.29: Shall I not visit for these things, sayth the Lord? or shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
5.30: An horrible and filthie thing is committed in the land.
5.31: The Prophets prophesie lies, and ye Priests receive giftes in their handes, and my people delite therein. What will ye then doe in the end thereof?

6.1: O ye children of Beniamin, prepare to flee out of the middes of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa: set up a standart upon Beth-haccerem: for a plague appeareth out of the North and great destruction.
6.2: I have compared the daughter of Zion to a beautiful and daintie woman.
6.3: The pastors with their flockes shall come unto her: they shall pitch their tentes round about by her, and every one shall feed in his place.
6.4: Prepare war against her: arise, and let us goe up toward the South: wo unto us: for the day declineth, and the shadowes of the evening are stretched out.
6.5: Arise, and let us goe up by night, and destroy her palaces.
6.6: For thus hath the Lord of hostes said, Hew down wood, and cast a mount against Jerusalem: this citie must be visited: all oppression is in the middes of it.
6.7: As the fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her malice: crueltie and spoyle is continually heard in her before me with sorowe and strokes.
6.8: Be thou instructed, O Jerusalem, lest my soul depart from thee, lest I make thee desolate as a land, that none inhabiteth.
6.9: Thus sayeth the Lord of hostes, They shall gather as a vine, the residue of Israel: turn back thine hand as the grape gatherer into the baskets.
6.10: Unto whom shall I speak, and admonish that they may hear? behold, their eares are uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken: behold, the word of the Lord is unto them as a reproche: they have no delite in it.
6.11: Therefore I am full of the wrath of the Lord: I am weary with holding it: I will powre it out upon the children in the street, and likewise upon the assembly of the yong men: for the husband shall even be taken with the wife, and the aged with him that is full of daies.
6.12: And their houses with their landes, and wives also shalbe turned unto strangers: for I will stretch out mine hand upon the inhabitants of the land, sayeth the Lord.
6.13: For from the least of them, even unto the greatest of them, every one is given unto couetousnesse, and from the Prophet even unto the Priest, they all deal falsely.
6.14: They have healed also ye hurt of the daughter of my people with sweet woordes, saying, Peace, peace, when there is no peace.
6.15: Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not ashamed, no neither could they have any shame: therefore they shall fall among the slain: when I shall visit them, they shall be cast down, sayth the Lord.
6.16: Thus sayeth the Lord, Stand in the waies and behold, and ask for the old way, which is the good way and walk therein, and yee shall find rest for your soules: but they said, We will not walk therein.
6.17: Also I set watchmen over you, which said, Take heed to the sound of the trumpet: but they said, We will not take heed.
6.18: Hear therefore, yee Gentiles, and thou Congregation know, what is among them.
6.19: Hear, O earth, behold, I will cause a plague to come upon this people, even the fruit of their own imaginations: because they have not taken heed unto my woordes, nor to my Law, but cast it off.
6.20: To what purpose bringest thou mee incense from Sheba, and sweet calamus from a far countrey? Your burnt offerings are not pleasant, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me.
6.21: Therefore thus sayeth the Lord, Behold, I will laie stumbling blockes before this people, and the fathers and the sonnes together shall fall upon them: the neighbour and his friend shall perish.
6.22: Thus sayeth the Lord, Behold, a people cometh from the North countrey, and a great nation shall arise from the sides of the earth.
6.23: With bow and shield shall they be weaponed: they are cruel and will have no compassion: their voyce roareth like the sea, and they ride upon horses, well appointed, like men of war against thee, O daughter Zion.
6.24: We have heard their fame, and our handes wax feeble sorrow is come upon us, as the sorrow of a woman in travail.
6.25: Goe not foorth into the field, nor walk by the way: for the sword of the enemie and fear is on every side.
6.26: O daughter of my people, gird thee with sackecloth, and wallow thy self in the ashes: make lamentation, and bitter mourning as for thine onely sonne: for the destroier shall suddenly come upon us.
6.27: I have set thee for a defence and fortress among my people, that thou maiest know and trie their waies.
6.28: They are all rebellious traitours, walking craftily: they are brass, and yron, they all are destroyers.
6.29: The bellowes are burnt: the lead is consumed in the fire: the founder melteth in vain: for the wicked are not taken away.
6.30: They shall call them reprobate silver, because the Lord hath reiected them.

7.1: The woordes that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
7.2: Stand in the gate of the Lordes house and crie this woorde there, and say, Hear the woorde of the Lord, all yee of Judah that enter in at these gates to worship the Lord.
7.3: Thus sayeth the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Amend your waies and your woorkes, and I will let you dwell in this place.
7.4: Trust not in lying woordes, saying, The Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord: this is the Temple of the Lord.
7.5: For if you amend and redresse your waies and your woorkes: if you execute iudgement between a man and his neighbour,
7.6: And oppress not the stranger, the fatherless and the widow and shed no innocent blood in this place, neither walk after other gods to your destruction,
7.7: Then will I let you dwell in this place in the land that I gave unto your fathers, for ever and ever.
7.8: Behold, you trust in lying woordes, that can not profit.
7.9: Will you steal, murder, and commit adulterie, and swear falsely and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom yee know not?
7.10: And come and stand before mee in this House, whereupon my Name is called, and say, We are delivered, though we have done all these abominations?
7.11: Is this House become a denne of theeues, whereupon my Name is called before your eyes? Behold, even I see it, sayeth the Lord.
7.12: But go ye now unto my place which was in Shilo, where I set my Name at the beginning, and behold, what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.
7.13: Therefore now because yee have done all these woorkes, sayeth the Lord, (and I rose up earely and spake unto you: but when I spake, yee would not hear me, neither when I called, would yee answer).
7.14: Therefore will I do unto this House, wherupon my Name is called, wherein also yee trust, even unto the place that I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done unto Shilo.
7.15: And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.
7.16: Therfore thou shalt not pray for this people, neither lift up crie or praier for them neither intreat me, for I will not hear thee.
7.17: Seest thou not what they doe in the cities of Judah and in the streetes of Jerusalem?
7.18: The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knede the dough to make cakes to the Queen of heaven and to powre out drink offrings unto other gods, that they may provoke me unto anger.
7.19: Doe they provoke me to anger, sayeth the Lord, and not themselves to the confusion of their own faces?
7.20: Therefore thus sayeth the Lord God, Behold, mine anger and my wrath shall be powred upon this place, upon man and upon beast, and upon the tree of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground, and it shall burn and not bee quenched.
7.21: Thus sayth the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat the flesh.
7.22: For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offrings and sacrifices.
7.23: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voyce, and I will be your God, and yee shalbe my people: and walk yee in all the wayes which I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.
7.24: But they would not obey, nor incline their ear, but went after the counsels and the stubbernesse of their wicked heart, and went backewarde and not forward.
7.25: Since the day that your fathers came up out of the land of Egypt, unto this day, I have even sent unto you al my servants the Prophets, rising up earely every day, and sending them.
7.26: Yet would they not hear me nor encline their ear, but hardened their neck and did worse then their fathers.
7.27: Therefore shalt thou speak al these words unto them, but they will not hear thee: thou shalt also crie unto them, but they will not answer thee.
7.28: But thou shalt say unto them, This is a nation that heareth not the voice of the Lord their God, nor receiveth discipline: trueth is perished, and is clean gone out of their mouth.
7.29: Cut off thine hear, O Jerusalem, and cast it away, and take up a complaint on the hie places: for the Lord hath reiected and forsaken the generation of his wrath.
7.30: For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, sayth the Lord: they have set their abominations in the House, whereupon my Name is called, to pollute it.
7.31: And they have built the hie place of Topheth, which is in the valley of Ben-Hinnom to burn their sonnes and their daughters in the fire, which I commanded them not, neither came it in mine heart.
7.32: Therefore behold, the dayes come, sayeth the Lord, that it shall no more be called Topheth, nor the valley of Ben-Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall burie in Topheth til there be no place.
7.33: And ye carkeises of this people shalbe meat for the foules of the heaven and for the beastes of the earth, and none shall fraie them away.
7.34: Then I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streetes of Jerusalem the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegrom and the voice of the bride: for the land shalbe desolate.

8.1: At that time, sayeth the Lord, they shall bring out the bones of the Kings of Judah, and the bones of their princes, and the bones of the Priests and the bones of the Prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem out of their graves.
8.2: And they shall spread them before the sunne and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and whom they have followed, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped: they shall not be gathered nor be buried, but shall be as doung upon the earth.
8.3: And death shall bee desired rather then life of all the residue that remaineth of this wicked familie, which remain in all the places where I have scattered them, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
8.4: Thou shalt say unto them also, Thus sayeth the Lord, Shall they fall and not arise? shall he turn away and not turn again?
8.5: Wherefore is this people of Jerusalem turned back by a perpetual rebellion? they gave themselves to deceit, and would not return.
8.6: I hearkened and heard, but none spake aright: no man repented him of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? every one turned to their race, as the horse rusheth into the battell.
8.7: Even the stork in the air knoweth her appointed times, and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming, but my people knoweth not the iudgement of the Lord.
8.8: How doe yee say, Wee are wise, and the Law of the Lord is with us? Loe, certeinly in vain made hee it, the penne of the scribes is in vain.
8.9: The wise men are ashamed: they are afraid and taken. loe, they have reiected the word of the Lord, and what wisdom is in them?
8.10: Therefore will I give their wives unto others, and their fieldes to them that shall possess them: for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to couetousnesse, and from the Prophet even unto the Priest, every one dealeth falsely.
8.11: For they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people with sweet woordes, saying, Peace, peace, when there is no peace.
8.12: Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not ashamed, neither could they have any shame: therefore shall they fall among the slain: when I shall visit them, they shall be cast down, sayeth the Lord.
8.13: I wil surely consume them, sayth the Lord: there shalbe no grapes on the vine, nor figges on the figtree, and the leaf shall fade, and the things that I have given them, shall depart from them.
8.14: Why doe we stay? assemble your selves, and let us enter into the strong cities, and let us be quiet there: for the Lord our God hath put us to silence and given us water with gall to drink, because we have sinned against the Lord.
8.15: We looked for peace, but no good came, and for a time of health, and behold troubles.
8.16: The neying of his horses was heard from Dan, the whole land trembled at the noyse of the neying of his strong horses: for they are come, and have deuoured the land with all that is in it, the citie, and those that dwell therein.
8.17: For behold, I will send serpents, and cockatrices among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall sting you, sayth the Lord.
8.18: I would have comforted my self against sorowe, but mine heart is heauie in me.
8.19: Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people for fear of them of a far countrey, Is not the Lord in Zion? is not her king in her? Why have they provoked mee to anger with their graven images, and with the vanities of a strange god?
8.20: The harvest is past, the sommer is ended, and we are not holpen.
8.21: I am sore vexed for the hurt of ye daughter of my people: I am heauie, and astonishment hath taken me.
8.22: Is there no balm at Gilead? is there no Physition there? Why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered.

9.1: Oh, that mine head were full of water and mine eyes a fountain of teares, that I might weep day and night for the slayne of the daughter of my people.
9.2: Oh, that I had in the wildernes a cottage of wayfaring men, that I might leave my people, and go from them: for they be all adulterers and an assembly of rebels,
9.3: And they bend their tongues like their bowes for lyes: but they have no courage for the trueth upon the earth: for they proceed from evil to worse, and they have not knowen mee, sayth the Lord.
9.4: Let every one take heed of his neighbour, and trust you not in any brother: for every brother will use deceit, and every friend will deal deceitfully,
9.5: And every one wil deceive his friend, and wil not speak the trueth: for they have taught their tongues to speak lies, and take great paynes to do wickedly.
9.6: Thine habitation is in the middes of deceivers: because of their deceit they refuse to know me, sayth the Lord.
9.7: Therefore thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Behold, I wil melt them, and trie them: for what should I els do for the daughter of my people?
9.8: Their tongue is as an arow shot out, and speaketh deceit: one speaketh peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth, but in his heart hee layeth wait for him.
9.9: Shal I not visit them for these things, saith the Lord? or shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
9.10: Upon the mountaines will I take up a weeping and a lamentation, and upon the fayre places of the wildernes a mourning, because they are burnt up: so that none can pass through them, neyther can men hear the voyce of the flock: both the fowl of the air, and the beast are fled away and gone.
9.11: And I wil make Jerusalem an heap, and a den of dragons, and I will make the cities of Judah waste, without an inhabitant.
9.12: Who is wise, to vnderstande this? and to whom the mouth of the Lord hath spoken, even he shall declare it. Why doth the land perish, and is burnt up like a wilderness, that none passeth through?
9.13: And the Lord sayeth, Because they have forsaken my Law, which I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice, neither walked thereafter,
9.14: But have walked after the stubbernesse of their own heart, and after Baalims, which their fathers taught them,
9.15: Therefore thus sayth the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Behold, I will feed this people with wormewood, and give them waters of gall to drink:
9.16: I wil scatter them also among the heathen, whom neither they nor their fathers have knowen, and I will send a sword after them, til I have consumed them.
9.17: Thus sayeth the Lord of hostes, Take heed, and call for the mourning women, that they may come, and send for skilful women that they may come,
9.18: And let them make haste, and let them take up a lamentation for us, that our eyes may cast out teares and our eye liddes gush out of water.
9.19: For a lamentable noyse is heard out of Zion, How are we destroyed, and utterly confounded, for we have forsaken the land, and our dwellings have cast us out.
9.20: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, O ye women, and let your eares regard the words of his mouth, and teach your daughters to mourn, and every one her neighbour to lament.
9.21: For death is come up into our windowes, and is entred into our palaces, to destroy the children without, and the yong men in the streetes.
9.22: Speak, thus sayth the Lord, The carkeises of men shall lye, even as the doung upon the field, and as the handful after the mower, and none shall gather them.
9.23: Thus saith the Lord, Let not the wise man glory in his wisedome, nor the strong man glorie in his strength, neyther the rich man glorie in his riches.
9.24: But let him that glorieth, glorie in this, that he understandeth, and knoweth me: for I am the Lord, which shew mercie, iudgement, and righteousnes in the earth: for in these things I delite, sayth the Lord.
9.25: Behold, the dayes come, sayth the Lord, that I wil visit all them, which are circumcised with the uncircumcised:
9.26: Egypt and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all the utmost corners of them that dwell in the wilderness: for all these nations are uncircumcised, and al the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart.

10.1: Hear ye the word of the Lord that he speaketh unto you, O house of Israel.
10.2: Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not afraid for the signes of heaven, though the heathen be afraid of such.
10.3: For the customes of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest (which is the work of the handes of the carpenter) with the axe,
10.4: And another decketh it with silver, and with gold: they fasten it with nailes, and hammers, that it fall not.
10.5: The idoles stand up as the palm tree, but speak not: they are borne because they cannot go fear them not, for they cannot do evil, neither can they do good.
10.6: There is none like unto thee, O Lord: thou art great, and thy name is great in power.
10.7: Who would not fear thee, O King of nations? for to thee appertaineth the dominion: for among all the wise men of the Gentiles, and in al their kingdomes there is none like thee.
10.8: But, altogether they dote, and are foolish: for the stock is a doctrine of vanitie.
10.9: Silver plates are brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, for the work of the workeman, and the handes of the founder: the blew silk, and the purple is their clothing: all these things are made by cunning men.
10.10: But the Lord is the God of trueth: he is the living God, and an everlasting King: at his anger the earth shall tremble, and the nations cannot abide his wrath.
10.11: (Thus shall you say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens)
10.12: He hath made the earth by his power, and established the world by his wisedome, and hath stretched out the heaven by his discretion.
10.13: Hee giveth by his voyce the multitude of waters in the heaven, and he causeth the cloudes to ascend from the endes of the earth: he turneth lightnings to rayne, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.
10.14: Every man is a beast by his own knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his melting is but falsehood, and there is no breath therein.
10.15: They are vanitie, and the work of errours: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.
10.16: The portion of Iaakob is not like them: for he is the maker of all things, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: the Lord of hostes is his Name.
10.17: Gather up thy wares out of the land, O thou that dwellest in the strong place.
10.18: For thus sayth the Lord, Behold, at this time I will throw as with a sling the inhabitants of the land, and will trouble them, and they shall find it so.
10.19: Wo is me for my destruction, and my grieuous plague: but I thought, Yet it is my sorow, and I will bear it.
10.20: My tabernacle is destroyed, and all my coardes are broken: my children are gone from me, and are not: there is none to spread out my tent any more, and to set up my curtaines.
10.21: For the Pastours are become beasts, and have not sought the Lord: therefore have they none understanding: and all the flockes of their pastures are scattered.
10.22: Behold, the noyse of the brute is come, and a great commotion out of the North countrey to make the cities of Judah desolate, and a denne of dragons.
10.23: O Lord, I know, that the way of man is not in himself, neyther is it in man to walk and to direct his steps.
10.24: O Lord, correct mee, but with iudgement, not in thine anger, least thou bring mee to nothing.
10.25: Powre out thy wrath upon the heathen, that know thee not, and upon the families that call not on thy Name: for they have eaten up Iaakob and deuoured him and consumed him, and have made his habitation desolate.

11.1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
11.2: Hear ye the wordes of this covenant, and speak unto the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
11.3: And say thou unto them, Thus sayeth the Lord God of Israel, Cursed be the man that obeyeth not the wordes of this covenant,
11.4: Which I commanded unto your fathers, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the yron fornace, saying, Obey my voyce, and doe according to all these things, which I command you: so shall ye be my people, and I will be your God,
11.5: That I may confirm the othe, that I have sworn unto your fathers, to give them a land, which floweth with milk and hony, as appeareth this day. Then answered I and sayde, So be it, O Lord.
11.6: Then the Lord said unto me, Cry all these words in the cities of Judah, and in the streetes of Jerusalem, saying, Hear yee the words of this covenant, and doe them.
11.7: For I have protested unto your fathers, whe I brought them up out of the land of Egypt unto this day, rising earely and protesting, saying, Obey my voyce.
11.8: Nevertheless they would not obey, nor encline their ear: but every one walked in the stubbernesse of his wicked heart: therefore I will bring upon them all the wordes of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did it not.
11.9: And the Lord sayd unto me, A conspiracie is found among the men of Judah, and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
11.10: They are turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers, which refused to hear my wordes: and they went after other gods to serve them: thus the house of Israel, and the house of Judah have broken my covenant, which I made with their fathers.
11.11: Therefore thus sayth the Lord, Behold, I will bring a plague upon them, which they shall not be able to escape, and though they cry unto me, I will not hear them.
11.12: Then shall the cities of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem goe, and crie unto the gods unto whom they offer incense, but they shall not bee able to help them in time of their trouble.
11.13: For according to the number of thy cities were thy gods, O Judah, and according to the number of the streetes of Jerusalem have yee set up altars of confusion, even altars to burn incense unto Baal.
11.14: Therfore thou shalt not pray for this people, neither lift up a crie, or prayer for them: for when they cry unto mee in their trouble, I will not hear them.
11.15: What should my beloved tarie in mine house, seeing they have committed abomination with manie? and the holy flesh goeth away from thee: yet when thou doest evil, thou reioycest.
11.16: The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: but with noyse and great tumult he hath set fyre upon it, and the branches of it are broken.
11.17: For the Lord of hostes that planted thee, hath pronounced a plague against thee, for the wickednes of the house of Israel, and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.
11.18: And the Lord hath taught me, and I know it, even then thou shewedst mee their practises.
11.19: But I was like a lamb, or a bullock, that is brought to the slaughter, and I knew not that they had devised thus against me, saying, Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof, and cut him out of the land of the living, that his name may be no more in memory.
11.20: But O Lord of hostes, that judgest righteously, and triest the reines and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I opened my cause.
11.21: The Lord therefore speaketh thus of the men of Anathoth, (that seek thy life, and say, Prophecie not in the Name of the Lord, that thou die not by our hands)
11.22: Thus therefore sayth the Lord of hostes, Behold, I will visit them: the yong men shall die by the sword: their sonnes and their daughters shall die by famine,
11.23: And none of them shall remain: for I will bring a plague upon the men of Anathoth, even the yeere of their visitation.

12.1: O Lord, if I dispute with thee, thou art righteous: yet let mee talk with thee of thy iudgements: wherefore doeth the way of the wicked prosper? why are all they in wealth that rebelliously transgress?
12.2: Thou hast planted them, and they have taken root: they grow, and bring forth fruit: thou art neere in their mouth, and far from their reines.
12.3: But thou, Lord, knowest me: thou hast seen me, and tried mine heart toward thee: pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare them for the day of slaughter.
12.4: How long shall the land mourn, and the herbes of every field wither, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein? the beastes are consumed and the birdes, because they sayd, He wil not see our last end.
12.5: If thou hast runne with the footemen and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou match thy self with horses? and if thou thoughtest thy self safe in a peaceable land, what wilt thou do in the swelling of Iorden?
12.6: For even thy brethren, and the house of thy father, even they have delt unfaithfully with thee, and they have cryed out altogether upon thee: but beleeue them not, though they speak fair to thee.
12.7: I have forsaken mine house: I have left mine heritage: I have given the dearely beloved of my soul into the hands of her enemies.
12.8: Mine heritage is unto mee, as a lion in the forest: it crieth out against mee, therefore have I hated it.
12.9: Shall mine heritage bee unto mee, as a bird of divers colours? are not the birdes about her, saying, Come, assemble all ye beastes of the field, come to eat her?
12.10: Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, and troden my portion under foot: of my pleasant portion they have made a desolate wilderness.
12.11: They have layde it waste, and it, being waste, mourneth unto me: and the whole land lyeth waste, because no man setteth his mind on it.
12.12: The destroyers are come upon all the high places in the wilderness: for the sword of the Lord shall deuoure from the one end of the land, even to the other end of the land: no flesh shall have peace.
12.13: They have sowen wheat, and reaped thornes: they were sick, and had no profit: and they were ashamed of your fruites, because of the fierce wrath of the Lord.
12.14: Thus sayeth the Lord against all mine evil neighbours, that touch the inheritance, which I have caused my people Israel to inherit, Behold, I will pluck them out of their land, and pluck out the house of Judah from among them.
12.15: And after that I have plucked them out, I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring again every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.
12.16: And if they will learn the wayes of my people, to swear by my Name, (The Lord liveth, as they taught my people to swear by Baal) then shall they be built in the middes of my people.
12.17: But if they will not obey, then will I utterly pluck up, and destroy that nation, sayeth the Lord.

13.1: Thus sayth the Lord unto mee, Goe, and buy thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loynes, and put it not in water.
13.2: So I bought the girdle according to the commandement of the Lord, and put it upon my loynes.
13.3: And the word of the Lord came unto me the second time, saying,
13.4: Take the girdle that thou hast bought, which is upon thy loynes, and arise, goe toward Perath, and hide it there in the cleft of the rock.
13.5: So I went, and hid it by Perath, as the Lord had commanded me.
13.6: And after many dayes, the Lord sayde unto mee, Arise, goe toward Perath, and take the girdle from thence, which I commanded thee to hide there.
13.7: Then went I to Perath, and digged, and took the girdle from the place where I had hid it, and behold, the girdle was corrupt, and was profitable for nothing.
13.8: Then the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
13.9: Thus sayth the Lord, After this maner will I destroy the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.
13.10: This wicked people have refused to hear my word, and walk after ye stubbernesse of their own heart, and walk after other gods to serve them, and to worship them: therefore they shalbe as this girdle, which is profitable to nothing.
13.11: For as the girdle cleaveth to the loynes of a man, so have I tied to me the whole house of Israel, and the whole house of Judah, saith the Lord, that they might bee my people: that they might have a name and prayse, and glory, but they would not hear.
13.12: Therefore thou shalt say unto them this word, Thus sayth the Lord God of Israel, Every bottell shalbe filled with wine, and they shall say unto thee, Doe we not know that every bottell shalbe filled with wine?
13.13: Then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the Kings that sit upon the throne of David, and the Priestes and the Prophets and all the inhabitantes of Jerusalem with drunkenness.
13.14: And I wil dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sonnes together, sayeth the Lord: I will not spare, I will not pitie nor have compassion, but destroy them.
13.15: Hear and give ear, be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken it.
13.16: Give glory to the Lord your God before he bring darknes, and or ever your feet stumble in the dark mountaines, and whiles you look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death and make it as darkenesse.
13.17: But if ye will not hear this, my soul shall weep in secret for your pride, and mine eye shall weep and drop down teares, because the Lords flock is caried away captive.
13.18: Say unto the King and to the Queen, Humble yourselues, sit down, for the crown of your glory shall come down from your heads.
13.19: The cities of the South shall be shut up, and no man shall open them: all Judah shall be caried away captive: it shall be wholy caried away captive.
13.20: Lift up your eyes and behold them that come from the North: where is the flock that was given thee, even thy beautiful flock?
13.21: What wilt thou say, when hee shall visit thee? (for thou hast taught them to be captaines and as chief over thee) shall not sorow take thee as a woman in travail?
13.22: And if thou say in thine heart, Wherefore come these things upon me? For the multitude of thine iniquities are thy skirts discovered and thy heeles made bare.
13.23: Can the black More change his skin? or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.
13.24: Therefore will I scatter them, as the stubble that is taken away with the South wind.
13.25: This is thy portion, and ye part of thy measures from me, sayth the Lord, because thou hast forgotten me and trusted in lyes.
13.26: Therefore I have also discovered thy skirts upon thy face, that thy shame may appear.
13.27: I have seen thine adulteries, and thy neiings, the filthiness of thy whoredom on the hils in the fieldes, and thine abominations. Wo unto thee, O Jerusalem: wilt thou not bee made clean? when shall it once be?

14.1: The word of the Lord that came unto Jeremiah, concerning the dearth.
14.2: Judah hath mourned, and the gates thereof are desolate, they have been brought to heaviness unto the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem goeth up.
14.3: And their nobles have sent their inferiours to the water, who came to the welles, and found no water: they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads.
14.4: For the ground was destroyed, because there was no rayne in the earth: the plowmen were ashamed, and covered their heads.
14.5: Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass.
14.6: And the wild asses did stand in the hygh places, and drew in their wind like dragons their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.
14.7: O Lord, though our iniquities testifie against us, deal with us according to thy name: for our rebellions are many, we sinned against thee.
14.8: O the hope of Israel, the sauiour thereof in the time of trouble, why art thou as a strager in ye land, as one that passeth by to tary for a night?
14.9: Why art thou as a man astonied, and as a strong man that cannot help? yet thou, O Lord, art in the middes of us, and thy Name is called upon us: forsake us not.
14.10: Thus saith the Lord unto this people, Thus have they delited to wander: they have not refrained their feet, therefore the Lord hath no delight in them: but he will now remember their iniquitie, and visit their sinnes.
14.11: Then sayd the Lord unto me, Thou shalt not pray to do this people good.
14.12: When they fast, I will not hear their cry, and when they offer burnt offering, and an oblation, I will not accept them: but I will consume them by the sword, and by the famine and by the pestilence.
14.13: Then answered I, Ah Lord God, behold, the prophets say unto them, Ye shall not see the sword, neither shall famine come upon you, but I wil give you assured peace in this place.
14.14: Then the Lord said unto me, The prophets prophecie lyes in my Name: I have not sent them, neither did I command them, neither spake I unto them, but they prophecie unto you a false vision, and divination, and vanitie, and deceitfulnes of their own heart.
14.15: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Concerning the prophets that prophecie in my Name, whom I have not sent, yet they say, Sword and famine shall not be in this land, by sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed.
14.16: And the people to whom these prophets doe prophecie, shalbe cast out in the streetes of Jerusalem, because of the famine, and the sword, and there shall be none to bury them, both they, and their wives, and their sonnes, and their daughters: for I wil powre their wickednes upon them.
14.17: Therefore thou shalt say this word unto them, Let mine eyes drop down teares night and day without ceasing: for the virgin daughter of my people is destroyed with a great destruction, and with a sore grieuous plague.
14.18: For if I go into the field, behold the slain with the sword: and if I enter into the citie, behold them that are sick for hunger also: moreover the Prophet also and the Priest go a wandring into a land that they know not.
14.19: Hast thou utterly reiected Judah, or hath thy soul abhorred Zion? why hast thou smitten us, that we cannot be healed? Wee looked for peace, and there is no good, and for the time of health, and behold trouble.
14.20: We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness and the iniquitie of our fathers: for we have sinned against thee.
14.21: Doe not abhorre us: for thy Names sake cast not down the throne of thy glory: remember and break not thy covenant with us.
14.22: Are there any among the vanities of the Gentiles, that can give rain? or can the heavens give showres? is it not thou, O Lord our God? therefore we will wait upon thee: for thou hast made all these things.

15.1: Then sayde the Lord unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before mee, yet mine affection could not be toward this people: cast them out of my sight, and let them depart.
15.2: And if they say unto thee, Whither shall we depart? then tell them, Thus saith the Lord, Such as are appointed to death, unto death: and such as are for the sword, to the sword: and such as are for the famine, to the famine: and such as are for the captiuitie, to the captiuitie.
15.3: And I wil appoint over them four kindes, sayth the Lord, the sword to slay, and the dogs to tear in pieces, and the soules of the heaven, and the beastes of the earth to deuoure, and to destroy.
15.4: I will scatter them also in all kingdomes of the earth, because of Manasseh the sonne of Hezekiah King of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.
15.5: Who shall then have pitie upon thee, O Jerusalem? or who shalbe sorie for thee? or who shall go to pray for thy peace?
15.6: Thou hast forsaken me, sayth the Lord, and gone backward: therefore wil I stretch out mine hand against thee, and destroy thee: for I am weary with repenting.
15.7: And I wil scatter them with the fanne in the gates of the earth I have wasted, and destroyed my people, yet they would not return from their wayes.
15.8: Their widdowes are increased by mee above the sand of the sea: I have brought upon them, and against the assembly of the yong men a destroyer at noon day: I have caused him to fal upon them, and the citie suddenly, and speedily.
15.9: She that hath borne seven, hath been made weak: her heart hath failed: the sunne hath failed her, whiles it was day: she hath been confounded, and ashamed, and the residue of them will I deliver unto the sword before their enemies, sayth the Lord.
15.10: Wo is mee, my mother, that thou hast borne mee, a contentious man, and a man that striveth with the whole earth I have neither lent on usury, nor men have lent unto me on vsurie: yet every one doeth curse me.
15.11: The Lord sayd, Surely thy remnant shall have wealth: surely I will cause thine enemie to intreat thee in the time of trouble, and in the time of affliction.
15.12: Shall the yron break the yron, and the brass that cometh from the North?
15.13: Thy substance and thy treasures wil I give to be spoyled without gain, and that for all thy sinnes even in all thy borders.
15.14: And I wil make thee to go with thine enemies into a land that thou knowest not: for a fire is kindled in mine anger, which shall burn you.
15.15: O Lord, thou knowest, remember me, and visit me, and revenge me of my persecuters: take mee not away in the continuance of thine anger: know that for thy sake I have suffered rebuke.
15.16: Thy wordes were found by me, and I did eat them, and thy word was unto me the joy and reioycing of mine heart: for thy Name is called upon me, O Lord God of hostes.
15.17: I sat not in the assembly of the mockers, neither did I reioyce, but sat alone because of thy plague: for thou hast filled me with indignation.
15.18: Why is mine heauines continual? and my plague desperate and cannot be healed? why art thou unto me as a lyar, and as waters that fail?
15.19: Therefore thus saith the Lord, If thou return, then wil I bring thee again, and thou shalt stand before me: and if thou take away the precious from the vile, thou shalt be according to my word: let them return unto thee, but return not thou unto them.
15.20: And I will make thee unto this people a strong brasen wall, and they shall fight against thee, but they shall not prevail against thee: for I am with thee to save thee and to deliver thee, saith ye Lord.
15.21: And I will deliver thee out of the hand of the wicked, and I will redeem thee out of the hand of the tyrants.

16.1: The word of the Lord came also unto mee, saying,
16.2: Thou shalt not take thee a wife, nor have sonnes nor daughters in this place.
16.3: For thus sayeth the Lord concerning the sonnes, and concerning the daughters that are borne in this place, and concerning their mothers that bear them, and concerning their fathers, that beget them in this land,
16.4: They shall die of deathes and diseases: they shall not be lamented, neither shall they be buried, but they shalbe as dung upon the earth, and they shalbe consumed by the sword, and by famine, and their carkeises shall be meat for the foules of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth.
16.5: For thus saith the Lord, Enter not into the house of mourning, neither goe to lament, nor be moved for the: for I have taken my peace, from this people, saith the Lord, even mercy and compassion.
16.6: Both the great, and the small shall die in this land: they shall not be buried, neither shall men lament for them nor cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for them.
16.7: They shall not stretch out the hands for the in the mourning to comfort them for the dead, neither shall they give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or for their mother.
16.8: Thou shalt not also goe into the house of feasting to sit with them to eat and to drink.
16.9: For thus sayth the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Behold, I wil cause to cease out of this place in your eyes, even in your dayes the voyce of myrth, and the voyce of gladnes, the voyce of the bridegrome and the voyce of the bride.
16.10: And when thou shalt shew this people all these wordes, and they shall say unto thee, Wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great plague against us? or what is our iniquitie? and what is our sinne that we have committed against the Lord our God?
16.11: Then shalt thou say unto them, Because your fathers have forsaken me, sayth the Lord, and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my Law,
16.12: (And ye have done worse then your fathers: for behold, you walk every one after the stubbernesse of his wicked heart, and will not hear me)
16.13: Therefore will I drive you out of this land into a land that ye know not, neither you, nor your fathers, and there shall ye serve other gods day and night: for I will shew you no grace.
16.14: Behold therfore, saith the Lord, the dayes come that it shall no more be sayde, The Lord liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt,
16.15: But the Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the North, and from all the landes where hee had scattered them, and I wil bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.
16.16: Behold, sayth the Lord, I wil send out many fishers, and they shall fish them, and after, will I send out many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain and from every hill, and out of the caves of the rockes.
16.17: For mine eyes are upon al their wayes: they are not hid from my face, neither is their iniquitie hid from mine eyes.
16.18: And first I will recompense their iniquitie and their sinne double, because they have defiled my land, and have filled mine inheritance with their filthie carions and their abominations.
16.19: O Lord, thou art my force, and my strength and my refuge in the day of affliction: the Gentiles shall come unto thee from the ends of the world, and shall say, Surely our fathers have inherited lies, and vanitie, wherein was no profit.
16.20: Shall a man make gods unto himself, and they are no gods?
16.21: Behold, therefore I will this once teach them: I will shew them mine hand and my power, and they shall know that my Name is the Lord.

17.1: The sinne of Judah is written with a pen of yron, and with the poynt of a diamond, and graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the hornes of your altars.
17.2: They remember their altars as their children, with their groves by the green trees upon the hilles.
17.3: O my mountain in the field, I will give thy substance, and all thy treasures to be spoyled, for the sinne of thy high places throughout all thy borders.
17.4: And thou shalt rest, and in thee shall be a rest from thine heritage that I gave thee, and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land, which thou knowest not: for yee have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.
17.5: Thus saith the Lord, Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and withdraweth his heart from the Lord.
17.6: For he shall be like the heath in the wilderness, and shall not see when any good cometh, but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land, and not inhabited.
17.7: Blessed be the man, that trusteth in ye Lord, and whose hope the Lord is.
17.8: For he shall be as a tree that is planted by the water, which spreadeth out her rootes by the river, and shall not feel when the heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green, and shall not care for the yeere of drought, neyther shall cease from yeelding fruit.
17.9: The heart is deceitful and wicked above all things, who can know it?
17.10: I the Lord search the heart, and try ye reines, even to give every man according to his wayes, and according to the fruit of his workes.
17.11: As the partryche gathereth the yong, which she hath not brought forth: so he that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the middes of his dayes, and at his end shall bee a fool.
17.12: As a glorious throne exalted from the beginning, so is the place of our Sanctuarie.
17.13: O Lord, the hope of Israel, all that forsake thee, shall be confounded: they that depart from thee, shalbe written in the earth, because they have forsaken the Lord, the fountain of living waters.
17.14: Heal me, O Lord, and I shall bee whole: save me, and I shall bee saved: for thou art my prayse.
17.15: Behold, they say unto me, Where is the word of the Lord? let it come now.
17.16: But I have not thrust in my self for a pastour after thee, neither have I desired the day of miserie, thou knowest: that which came out of my lips, was right before thee.
17.17: Be not terrible unto mee: thou art mine hope in the day of aduersitie.
17.18: Let them bee confounded, that persecute me, but let not me be confounded: let them be afraid, but let not me be afraid: bring upon them the day of aduersitie, and destroy them with double destruction.
17.19: Thus hath the Lord said unto me, Goe and stand in the gate of the children of the people, whereby the Kings of Judah come in, and by the which they goe out, and in all ye gates of Jerusalem,
17.20: And say unto them, Hear the word of the Lord, ye Kings of Judah, and al Judah, and all the inhabitants of Ierusale, that enter in by these gates.
17.21: Thus sayth the Lord, Take heed to your soules, and bear no burden in the Sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem.
17.22: Neither cary foorth burdens out of your houses in the Sabbath day: neither doe yee any work, but sanctifie the Sabbath, as I commanded your fathers.
17.23: But they obeied not, neither inclined their eares, but made their neckes stiff and would not hear, nor receive correction.
17.24: Nevertheless if ye will hear me, sayth the Lord, and bear no burden through the gates of the citie in the Sabbath day, but sanctifie ye Sabbath day, so that ye do no work therein,
17.25: Then shall the Kings and the princes enter in at the gates of this citie, and shall sit upon the throne of David, and shall ride upon charets, and upon horses, both they and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and this citie shall remain for ever.
17.26: And they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from about Jerusalem, and from the land of Beniamin, and from the plain, and from the mountaines, and from the South, which shall bring burnt offrings, and sacrifices, and meat offrings, and incense, and shall bring sacrifice of prayse into the house of the Lord.
17.27: But if ye will not hear me to sanctifie the Sabbath day, and not to bear a burden nor to go through the gates of Jerusalem in the Sabbath day, then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall deuoure the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.

18.1: The word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
18.2: Arise, and go down into the potters house, and there shall I shew thee my words.
18.3: Then I went down to the potters house, and behold, he wrought a work on the wheeles.
18.4: And the vessell that he made of clay, was broken in the hand of the potter. so he returned, and made it another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
18.5: Then the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
18.6: O house of Israel, cannot I doe with you as this potter, sayth the Lord? behold, as the clay is in the potters hand, so are you in mine hand, O house of Israel.
18.7: I will speak suddenly against a nation or against a kingdom to pluck it up, and to root it out and to destroy it.
18.8: But if this nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their wickedness, I will repent of the plague that I thought to bring upon them.
18.9: And I wil speak suddenly concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom to build it and to plant it.
18.10: But if it do evil in my sight and hear not my voyce, I will repent of ye good that I thought to do for them.
18.11: Speak thou now therefore unto the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith ye Lord, Behold, I prepare a plague for you, and purpose a thing against you: return you therefore every one from his evil way, and make your wayes and your workes good.
18.12: But they sayde desperately, Surely wee will walk after our own imaginations, and doe every man after the stubburnnesse of his wicked heart.
18.13: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Ask now among the heathen, who hath heard such thinges? the virgin of Israel hath done very filthily.
18.14: Will a man forsake the snow of Lebanon, which cometh from the rock of the field? or shall the cold flowing waters, that come from another place, be forsaken?
18.15: Because my people hath forgotten me, and have burnt incense to vanitie, and their prophets have caused them to stumble in their wayes from the auncient wayes, to walk in the pathes and way that is not troden,
18.16: To make their land desolate and a perpetual derision, so that every one that passeth thereby, shalbe astonished and wagge his head,
18.17: I will scatter them with an East wind before the enemie: I will shew them the back, and not the face in the day of their destruction.
18.18: Then sayde they, Come, and let us imagine some device against Jeremiah: for the Law shall not perish from the Priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the Prophet: come, and let us smite him with the tongue, and let us not give heed to any of his words.
18.19: Hearken unto mee, O Lord, and hear the voyce of them that contend with me.
18.20: Shall evil be recompensed for good? for they have digged a pit for my soul: remember that I stood before thee, to speak good for the, and to turn away thy wrath from them.
18.21: Therefore, deliver up their children to famine, and let them drop away by the force of the sword, and let their wives be robbed of their children, and be widowes: and let their husbands be put to death, and let their yong men be slayne by the sword in the battell.
18.22: Let the cry bee heard from their houses, when thou shalt bring an host suddenly upon them: for they have digged a pit to take me, and hid snares for my feet.
18.23: Yet Lord thou knowest al their counsel against me tendeth to death: forgive not their iniquitie, neither put out their sinne from thy sight, but let them be ouerthrowen before thee: deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.

19.1: Thus sayth the Lord, Goe, and buy an earthen bottel of a potter, and take of the ancients of the people, and of the ancients of the Priests,
19.2: And goe forth unto the valley of Ben-hinnom, which is by the entrie of the East gate: and thou shalt preach there the wordes, that I shall tell thee,
19.3: And shalt say, Hear yee the word of the Lord, O Kings of Judah, and inhabitantes of Jerusalem, Thus sayth the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Behold, I will bring a plague upon this place, the which whosoever heareth, his eares shall tingle.
19.4: Because they have forsaken me, and prophaned this place, and have burnt incense in it unto other gods, whom neyther they, nor their fathers have knowen, nor the Kings of Judah (they have filled this place also with the blood of innocents,
19.5: And they have built the hie places of Baal, to burn their sonnes with fire for burnt offrings unto Baal, which I commanded not, nor spake it, neither came it into my mind)
19.6: Therefore behold, the dayes come, sayth the Lord, that this place shall no more be called Topheth, nor ye valley of Ben-hinnom, but the valley of slaughter.
19.7: And I will bring the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem to nought in this place, and I will cause them to fall by the sword before their enemies, and by the hand of them that seek their lives: and their carkeises will I give to be meat for ye foules of the heaven, and to the beastes of the field.
19.8: And I will make this citie desolate and an hissing, so that every one that passeth thereby, shalbe astonished and hiss because of all ye plagues thereof.
19.9: And I will feed the with the flesh of their sonnes and with the flesh of their daughters, and every one shall eat the flesh of his friend in the siege and straitness, wherewith their enemies that seek their lives, shall hold them strait.
19.10: Then shalt thou break the bottell in the sight of the men that go with thee,
19.11: And shalt say unto them, Thus saith ye Lord of hostes, Even so will I break this people and this citie, as one breaketh a potters vessell, that cannot be made whole again, and they shall bury them in Topheth till there be no place to bury.
19.12: Thus will I doe unto this place, sayth the Lord, and to the inhabitantes thereof, and I will make this citie like Topheth.
19.13: For the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses of the Kings of Judah shalbe defiled as the place of Topheth, because of al the houses upon whose roofes they have burnt incense unto all the host of heaven, and have powred out drink offerings unto other gods.
19.14: Then came Jeremiah from Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophecie, and he stood in the court of the Lordes house, and sayde to all the people,
19.15: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Behold, I will bring upon this citie, and upon all her townes, all the plagues that I have pronounced against it, because they have hardened their neckes, and would not hear my wordes.

20.1: When Pashur, the sonne of Immer, the Priest, which was appointed gouernour in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophecied these things,
20.2: Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the Prophet, and put him in the stockes that were in the hie gate of Beniamin which was by the House of the Lord.
20.3: And on the morning, Pashur brought Jeremiah out of the stockes. Then said Jeremiah unto him, The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor-missabib.
20.4: For thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will make thee to be a terrour to thy self, and to al thy friends, and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it, and I will give all Judah into the hand of the King of Babel, and he shall cary them captive into Babel, and shall slay them with the sword.
20.5: Moreover, I will deliver all the substance of this citie, and all the labours thereof, and al the precious things thereof, and all the treasures of the Kings of Judah will I give into the hand of their enemies, which shall spoyle them, and take them away and cary them to Babel.
20.6: And thou Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house, shall go into captiuitie, and thou shalt come to Babel, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buryed there, thou and all thy friendes, to whom thou hast prophecied lyes.
20.7: O Lord, thou hast deceived me, and I am deceived: thou art stronger then I, and hast prevailed: I am in derision daily: every one mocketh me.
20.8: For since I spake, I cryed out of wrong, and proclaimed desolation: therefore the word of the Lord was made a reproche unto me, and in derision daily.
20.9: Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his Name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.
20.10: For I had heard the railing of many, and fear on every side. Declare, said they, and wee wil declare it: all my familiars watched for mine halting, saying, It may be that he is deceived: so we shall prevail against him, and we shall execute our vengeance upon him.
20.11: But the Lord is with me like a mightie gyant: therefore my persecuters shall be ouerthrowen, and shall not prevail, and shalbe greatly confounded: for they have done vnwisely, and their everlasting shame shall never be forgotten.
20.12: But, O Lord of hostes, that tryest the righteous, and seest the reines and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I opened my cause.
