20.13: Sing unto the Lord, praise ye the Lord: for he hath delivered the soul of the poor from the hand of the wicked.
20.14: Cursed be the day wherein I was borne: and let not the day wherein my mother bare me, be blessed.
20.15: Cursed be the man, that shewed my father, saying, A man child is borne unto thee, and comforted him.
20.16: And let that man be as the cities, which the Lord hath ouerturned and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the showting at noon tide,
20.17: Because he hath not slain me, even from the womb, or that my mother might have been my grave, or her wobe a perpetual conception.
20.18: How is it, that I came forth of the womb, to see labour and sorowe, that my dayes should be consumed with shame?

21.1: The word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, when king Zedekiah sent unto him Pashur, the sonne of Malchiah, and Zephaniah, the sonne of Maaseiah the Priest, saying,
21.2: Inquire, I pray thee, of the Lord for us, (for Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel maketh war against us) if so be that the Lord will deal with us according to all his wonderous workes, that he may return up from us.
21.3: Then said Jeremiah, Thus shall you say to Zedekiah,
21.4: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands, wherewith ye fight against the King of Babel, and against the Caldeans, which besiege you without the walles, and I will assemble them into the middes of this citie.
21.5: And I my self will fight against you with an outstretched hand, and with a mighty arm, eve in anger and in wrath, and in great indignation.
21.6: And I will smite the inhabitants of this citie, both man, and beast: they shall die of a great pestilence.
21.7: And after this, sayeth the Lord, I will deliver Zedekiah the King of Judah, and his servants, and the people, and such as are left in this citie, from the pestilence, from the sword and from the famine into the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel, and into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those that seek their lives, and he shall smite them with the edge of the sword: he shall not spare them, neither have pitie nor compassion.
21.8: And unto this people thou shalt say, Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.
21.9: He that abideth in this citie, shall dye by the sword and by the famine, and by the pestilence: but he that goeth out, and falleth to the Caldeans, that besiege you, he shall live, and his life shalbe unto him for a pray.
21.10: For I have set my face against this citie, for evil and not for good, saith the Lord: it shalbe given into the hand of the King of Babel, and he shall burn it with fire.
21.11: And say unto the house of the King of Judah, Hear ye the word of the Lord.
21.12: O house of David, thus saith the Lord, Execute iudgement in the morning, and deliver the oppressed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest my wrath go out like fire and burn, that none can quench it, because of the wickednes of your workes.
21.13: Behold, I come against thee, O inhabitant of the valley, and rock of the plain, saith the Lord, which say, Who shall come down against us? or who shall enter into our habitations?
21.14: But I will visit you according to the fruit of your workes, saith the Lord, and I will kindle a fire in the forest thereof, and it shall deuoure round about it.

22.1: Thus said the Lord, Goe down to the house of the King of Judah, and speak there this thing,
22.2: And say, Hear the word of the Lord, O King of Judah, that sittest upon the throne of David, thou and thy servants, and thy people that enter in by these gates.
22.3: Thus saith the Lord, Execute ye iudgement and righteousnes, and deliver the oppressed from the hand of the oppressor, and vex not the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow: doe no violence, nor sheade innocent blood in this place.
22.4: For if ye do this thing, then shall the kings sitting upon the throne of David enter in by the gates of this House, and ride upon charets, and upon horses, both he and his servants and his people.
22.5: But if ye will not hear these wordes, I swear by my self, saith the Lord, that this House shalbe waste.
22.6: For thus hath the Lord spoken upon the Kings house of Judah, Thou art Gilead unto me, and the head of Lebanon, yet surely I wil make thee a wildernes and as cities not inhabited,
22.7: And I will prepare destroyers against thee, every one with his weapons, and they shall cut down thy chief cedar trees, and cast them in the fire.
22.8: And many nations shall pass by this citie, and they shall say every man to his neighbour, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this great citie?
22.9: Then shall they answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord their God, and worshipped other gods, and served them.
22.10: Weep not for the dead, and be not moved for them, but weep for him that goeth out: for he shall return no more, nor see his native countrey.
22.11: For thus saith ye Lord, As touching Shallum the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, which reigned for Josiah his father, which went out of this place, he shall not return thither,
22.12: But he shall die in the place, whither they have ledde him captive, and shall see this land no more.
22.13: Wo unto him that buildeth his house by vnrighteousnesse, and his chambers without equitie: he useth his neighbour without wages, and giveth him not for his work.
22.14: He saith, I will build me a wide house and large chambers: so he will make him self large windowes, and feeling with cedar, and paint them with vermilion.
22.15: Shalt thou reign, because thou closest thy self in cedar? did not thy father eat and drink and prosper, when he executed iudgement and justice?
22.16: When he judged the cause of the afflicted and the poor, he prospered: was not this because he knew me, saith the Lord?
22.17: But thine eyes and thine heart are but only for thy couetousnesse, and for to sheade innocent blood, and for oppression, and for destruction, even to doe this.
22.18: Therefore thus saith the Lord against Jehoiakim, the sonne of Josiah king of Judah, They shall not lament him, saying, Ah, my brother, or ah, sister: neither shall they mourn for him, saying, Ah, lord, or ah, his glorie.
22.19: He shalbe buryed, as an ass is buryed, even drawen and cast foorth without the gates of Jerusalem.
22.20: Goe up to Lebanon, and cry: showte in Bashan and cry by the passages: for all thy lovers are destroyed.
22.21: I spake unto thee when thou wast in prosperitie: but thou saidest, I will not hear: this hath been thy maner from thy youth, that thou wouldest not obey my voyce.
22.22: The wind shall feed all thy pastors, and thy lovers shall goe into captiuitie: and then shalt thou be ashamed and confounded of al thy wickedness.
22.23: Thou that dwellest in Lebanon, and makest thy nest in the cedars, how beautiful shalt thou be when sorowes come upon thee, as the sorowe of a woman in travail?
22.24: As I live, saith the Lord, though Coniah the sonne of Jehoiakim King of Judah, were the signet of my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence.
22.25: And I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and into the hand of them, whose face thou fearest, even into the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar king of Babel, and into the hand of the Caldeans.
22.26: And I will cause them to cary thee away, and thy mother that bare thee, into another countrey, where ye were not borne, and there shall ye die.
22.27: But to the land, whereunto they desire to return, they shall not return thither.
22.28: Is not this man Coniah as a despised and broken idol? or as a vessell, wherein is no pleasure? wherefore are they caryed away, hee and his seed, and cast out into a land that they know not?
22.29: O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord.
22.30: Thus saith the Lord, Write this man destitute of children, a man that shall not prosper in his dayes: for there shall be no man of his seed that shall prosper and sit upon the throne of David, or bear rule any more in Judah.

23.1: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, saith the Lord.
23.2: Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel unto the pastors that feed my people, Yee have scattered my flock and thrust them out, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit you for the wickedness of your works, saith the Lord.
23.3: And I will gather the remnant of my sheep out of all countreyes, whither I had driven them, and will bring them again to their foldes, and they shall grow and encrease.
23.4: And I will set up shepheardes over them, which shall feed them: and they shall dread no more nor be afraid, neither shall any of them be lacking, saith the Lord.
23.5: Behold, The dayes come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous branch, and a King shall reign, and prosper, and shall execute iudgement, and justice in the earth.
23.6: In his dayes Judah shalbe saved, and Israel shall dwell safely, and this is the Name wherby they shall call him, The Lord our righteousness.
23.7: Therefore behold, the dayes come, sayth the Lord, that they shall no more say, The Lord liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt,
23.8: But the Lord liveth, which brought up and led the seed of the house of Israel out of the North countrey and from all countryes where I had scattered them, and they shall dwell in their own land.
23.9: Mine heart breaketh within mee, because of the prophets, all my bones shake: I am like a drunken man (and like a man whom wine hath overcome) for the presence of the Lord and for his holie wordes.
23.10: For the land is full of adulterers, and because of othes the land mourneth, the pleasant places of the wilderness are dried up, and their course is evil, and their force is not right.
23.11: For both the prophet and the Priest doe wickedly: and their wickedness have I found in mine House, saith the Lord.
23.12: Wherefore their way shalbe unto them as slipperie wayes in the darkness: they shalbe driven foorth and fall therein: for I will bring a plague upon them, even the yeere of their visitation, saith the Lord.
23.13: And I have seen foolishness in the prophets of Samaria, that prophecied in Baal, and caused my people Israel to ere.
23.14: I have seen also in the prophets of Jerusalem filthines: they commit adulterie and walk in lies: they strengthen also the hands of the wicked that none can return from his wickedness: they are all unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorah.
23.15: Therefore thus saith the Lord of hostes concerning the prophets, Behold, I will feed them with wormewood, and make them drink the water of gall: for from the prophets of Jerusalem is wickedness gone forth into all the land.
23.16: Thus sayth ye Lord of hosts, Hear not the wordes of the prophets that prophecie unto you, and teach you vanitie: they speak the vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.
23.17: They say still unto them that despise mee, The Lord hath sayde, Ye shall have peace: and they say unto every one that walketh after the stubbernesse of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you.
23.18: For who hath stand in the counsel of the Lord that he hath perceived and heard his word? Who hath marked his word and heard it?
23.19: Behold, the tempest of the Lord goeth forth in his wrath, and a violent whirlewinde shall fall down upon the head of the wicked.
23.20: The anger of the Lord shall not return until he have executed, and till he have perfourmed the thoughts of his heart: in the latter dayes ye shall vnderstande it plainely.
23.21: I have not sent these prophets, sayth the Lord, yet they ranne; I have not spoken to them, and yet they prophecied.
23.22: But if they had stand in my counsel, and had declared my words to my people, then they should have turned them from their evil way, and from the wickedness of their inventions.
23.23: Am I a God at hand, saith the Lord, and not a God far off?
23.24: Can any hide him self in secret places, that I shall not see him, sayth the Lord? Do not I fill heaven and earth, saieth the Lord?
23.25: I have heard what the prophets said, that prophecie lies in my Name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
23.26: How long? Doe the prophets delite to prophecie lies, even prophecying the deceit of their own heart?
23.27: Think they to cause my people to forget my Name by their dreames, which they tell every man to his neyghbour, as their forefathers have forgotten my Name for Baal?
23.28: The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream, and hee that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully: what is the chaff to the wheat, sayth the Lord?
23.29: Is not my word even like a fire, sayeth the Lord? and like an hammer, that breaketh the stone?
23.30: Therefore behold, I will come against the prophets, saieth the Lord, that steal my word euerie one from his neighbour.
23.31: Behold, I will come against the prophets, saith the Lord, which have sweet tongues, and say, He saith.
23.32: Behold, I will come against them that prophecie false dreames, saith the Lord, and doe tell them, and cause my people to ere by their lies, and by their flatteries, and I sent them not, nor commanded them: therefore they bring no profit unto this people, saith the Lord.
23.33: And when this people, or the prophet, or a Priest shall ask thee, saying, What is the burden of the Lord? thou shalt then say unto them, What burden? I will even forsake you, saith the Lord.
23.34: And the prophet, or the Priest, or the people that shall say, The burden of the Lord, I will even visit euerie such one, and his house.
23.35: Thus shall yee say every one to his neighbour, and euerie one to his brother, What hath the Lord answered? and what hath the Lord spoken?
23.36: And the burden of the Lord shall yee mention no more: for every mans word shall bee his burden: for ye have perverted the words of the living God, the Lord of hostes our God.
23.37: Thus shalt thou say to the Prophet, What hath the Lord answered thee? and what hath the Lord spoken?
23.38: And if you say, The burden of the Lord, Then thus saith the Lord, Because yee say this word, The burden of the Lord, and I have sent unto you, saying, Ye shall not say, The burden of the Lord,
23.39: Therefore behold, I, even I will utterly forget you, and I will forsake you, and the citie that I gave you and your fathers, and cast you out of my presence,
23.40: And will bring an everlasting reproche upon you, and a perpetual shame which shall never be forgotten.

24.1: The Lord shewed me, and behold, two baskets of figges were set before the Temple of the Lord, after that Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel had caryed away captive Jeconiah ye sonne of Jehoiakim King of Judah, and the princes of Judah with the workemen, and cunning men of Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babel.
24.2: One basket had verie good figges, even like the figges that are first ripe: and the other basket had verie naughtie figges, which could not be eaten, they were so evil.
24.3: Then said the Lord unto mee, What seest thou, Jeremiah? And I said, Figges: ye good figges verie good, and the naughtie verie naughtie, which cannot be eaten, they are so evil.
24.4: Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
24.5: Thus sayeth the Lord, the God of Israel, Like these good figges, so will I know them that are caryed away captive of Judah to bee good, whom I have sent out of this place, into the land of the Caldeans.
24.6: For I wil set mine eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them again to this land, and I will build them, and not destroy them, and I will plant them, and not root them out,
24.7: And I will give them an heart to know me, that I am the Lord, and they shalbe my people, and I wil be their God: for they shall return unto mee with their whole heart.
24.8: And as the naughtie figges which can not bee eaten, they are so evil (surely thus saith the Lord) so wil I give Zedekiah the King of Judah, and his princes, and the residue of Jerusalem, that remain in this land, and them that dwell in the land of Egypt:
24.9: I will even give them for a terrible plague to all the kingdomes of the earth, and for a reproche, and for a proverb, for a common talk, and for a curse, in all places where I shall cast them.
24.10: And I will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence among them, till they bee consumed out of the land, that I gave unto them and to their fathers.

25.1: The word that came to Jeremiah, concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth yeere of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah that was in the first yeere of Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel:
25.2: The which Jeremiah the Prophet spake unto all the people of Judah, and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying,
25.3: From the thirteenth yeere of Josiah the sonne of Amon King of Judah, even unto this day (that is the three and twentieth yeere) the word of the Lord hath come unto mee, and I have spoken unto you rising earely and speaking, but ye would not hear.
25.4: And the Lord hath sent unto you all his seruantes the Prophets, rising early and sending them, but yee would not hear, nor encline your eares to obey.
25.5: They sayde, Turn again now every one from his evil way, and from the wickednes of your inventions, and ye shall dwell in the land that the Lord hath given unto you, and to your fathers for ever and ever.
25.6: And go not after other gods to serve them and to worshippe them, and provoke me not to anger with the workes of your hands, and I will not punish you.
25.7: Nevertheless ye would not hear me, saith the Lord, but have provoked mee to anger with the workes of your hands to your own hurt.
25.8: Therefore thus saith the Lord of hostes, Because ye have not heard my wordes,
25.9: Behold, I will send and take to mee all the families of the North, saith the Lord, and Nebuchad-nezzar the King of Babel my servant, and will bring them against this land, and against the inhabitantes thereof, and against all these nations round about, and will destroy them, and make them an astonishment and an hissing, and a continual desolation.
25.10: Moreover I will take from them the voyce of mirth and the voyce of gladness, the voyce of the bridegrome and the voyce of the bride, the noise of the milstones, and the light of the candle.
25.11: And this whole land shalbe desolate, and an astonishment, and these nations shall serve the King of Babel seuentie yeeres.
25.12: And when the seuentie yeres are accomplished, I will visit the King of Babel and that nation, saith the Lord, for their iniquities, even the land of the Caldeans, and will make it a perpetual desolation,
25.13: And I will bring upon that land all my wordes which I have pronounced against it, even all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah hath prophecied against all nations.
25.14: For many nations, and great Kings shall even serve themselves of them: thus will I recompense them according to their deedes, and according to the workes of their own handes.
25.15: For thus hath the Lord God of Israel spoken unto me, Take the cuppe of wine of this mine indignation at mine hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.
25.16: And they shall drink, and be moved and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them.
25.17: Then took I the cup at the Lordes hand, and made all people to drink, unto whom the Lord had sent me:
25.18: Even Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and the Kings thereof, and the princes thereof, to make them desolate, an astonishment, an hissing, and a curse, as appeareth this day:
25.19: Pharaoh also, King of Egypt, and his servants, and his princes, and all his people:
25.20: And all sortes of people, and all the Kings of the land of Uz: and all the Kings of the land of the Philistims, and Ashkelon, and Azzah, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod:
25.21: Edom, and Moab, and the Ammonites,
25.22: And all the Kings of Tyrus, and all the kings of Zidon, and the Kings of the Yles, that are beyond the Sea,
25.23: And Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all that dwell in the uttermost corners,
25.24: And all the Kings of Arabia, and all the Kings of Arabia, that dwell in the desert,
25.25: And all the Kings of Zimri, and all the Kings of Elam, and all the Kings of the Medes,
25.26: And all the Kings of the North, far and neere one to another, and all the kingdomes of the world, which are upon the earth, and the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.
25.27: Therefore say thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Drink and bee drunken, and spewe and fall, and rise no more, because of the sword, which I will send among you.
25.28: But if they refuse to take the cuppe at thine hand to drink, then tell them, Thus saith the Lord of hostes, Ye shall certainely drink.
25.29: For loe, I beginne to plague the citie, where my Name is called upon, and should you goe free? Ye shall not goe quite: for I will call for a sword upon al the inhabitants of the earth, saith the Lord of hostes.
25.30: Therefore prophecie thou against them al these words, and say unto them, The Lord shall roar from above, and thrust out his voyce from his holy habitation: he shall roar upon his habitation, and crie aloud, as they that press the grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.
25.31: The sound shall come to the endes of the earth: for the Lord hath a controuersie with the nations, and will enter into iudgement with all flesh, and he will give them that are wicked, to the sword, saith the Lord.
25.32: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, Behold, a plague shall goe foorth from nation to nation, and a great whirlewinde shalbe raised up from the coastes of the earth,
25.33: And the slain of the Lord shall be at that day, from one end of the earth, even unto the other end of the earth: they shall not bee mourned, neither gathered nor buried, but shalbe as the dongue upon the ground.
25.34: Howl, ye shepherdes, and crie, and wallow your selves in the ashes, ye principal of the flock: for your dayes of slaughter are accomplished, and of your dispersion, and ye shall fall like precious vessels.
25.35: And the flight shall fail from the shepherdes, and the escaping from the principal of the flock.
25.36: A voyce of the cry of the shepherdes, and an howling of the principal of the flock shalbe heard: for the Lord hath destroyed their pasture.
25.37: And the best pastures are destroyed because of the wrath and indignation of the Lord.
25.38: He hath forsaken his covert, as the lyon: for their land is waste, because of the wrath of the oppressor, and because of ye wrath of his indignatio.

26.1: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, came this word from the Lord, saying,
26.2: Thus saith the Lord, Sand in the court of the Lordes House, and speak unto all the cities of Judah, which come to worshippe in the Lords House, all the wordes that I commaund thee to speak unto them: keep not a word back,
26.3: If so be they will hearken, and turn every man from his evil way, that I may repent me of the plague, which I have determined to bring upon them, because of the wickedness of their workes.
26.4: And thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord, If ye will not hear me to walk in my Lawes, which I have set before you,
26.5: And to hear ye wordes of my servants the Prophets, whom I sent unto you, both rising up earely, and sending them, and will not obey them,
26.6: Then will I make this House like Shiloh, and will make this citie a curse to all the nations of the earth.
26.7: So the Priestes, and the Prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these wordes in the House of the Lord.
26.8: Now when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to speak unto all the people, then the Priestes, and the prophets, and all the people took him, and said, Thou shalt die the death.
26.9: Why hast thou prophecied in the Name of the Lord, saying, This House shall be like Shiloh, and this citie shalbe desolate without an inhabitant? and all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the House of the Lord.
26.10: And when the princes of Judah heard of these things, they came up from the Kings house into the House of the Lord, and sat down in the entrie of the new gate of the Lords House.
26.11: Then spake the Priestes, and the prophets unto the princes, and to all the people, saying, This man is worthie to die: for he hath prophecied against this citie, as ye have heard with your eares.
26.12: Then spake Jeremiah unto all the princes, and to al the people, saying, The Lord hath sent me to prophecie against this house and against this citie all the things that ye have heard.
26.13: Therefore now amend your wayes and your workes, and hear the voyce of the Lord your God, that the Lord may repent him of the plague, that he hath pronounced against you.
26.14: As for me, behold, I am in your hands: do with me as ye think good and right.
26.15: But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon your selves, and upon this citie, and upon the inhabitants thereof: for of a trueth the Lord hath sent me unto you, to speak all these words in your eares.
26.16: Then said the princes and all the people unto the Priestes, and to the prophets, This man is not worthie to die: for he hath spoken unto us in the Name of the Lord our God.
26.17: Then rose up certain of the Elders of the land, and spake to all the assemblie of the people, saying,
26.18: Michah the Morashite prophecied in the dayes of Hezekiah king of Judah, and spake to al the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hostes, Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shalbe an heap, and the mountain of the House shalbe as the hie places of the forest.
26.19: Did Hezekiah King of Judah, and all Judah put him to death? did he not fear ye Lord, and prayed before the Lord, and the Lord repented him of the plague, that he had pronounced against them? Thus might we procure great evil against our soules.
26.20: And there was also a man that prophecied in the Name of the Lord, one Vriiah the sonne of Shemaiah, of Kiriath-iarem, who prophecied against this citie, and against this land, according to all the wordes of Jeremiah.
26.21: Now when Jehoiakim the King with all his men of power, and all the princes heard his wordes, the King sought to slay him. But when Vriiah heard it, he was afraid and fled, and went into Egypt.
26.22: Then Jehoiakim the King sent men into Egypt, even Elnathan the sonne of Achbor, and certain with him into Egypt.
26.23: And they fet Vriiah out of Egypt, and brought him unto Jehoiakim the King, who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead bodie into the graves of the children of the people.
26.24: But the hand of Ahikam the sonne of Shaphan was with Jeremiah that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.

27.1: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
27.2: Thus saith the Lord to me, Make thee bonds, and yokes, and put them upon thy neck,
27.3: And send them to the King of Edom, and to the King of Moab, and to the King of the Ammonites, and to the King of Tyrus, and to the king of Zidon, by the hand of the messengers which come to Ierusale unto Zedekiah ye king of Judah,
27.4: And command them to say unto their masters, Thus saith the Lord of hostes the God of Israel, Thus shall ye say unto your masters,
27.5: I have made the earth, the man, and the beast that are upon the groud, by my great power, and by my outstreched arm, and have given it unto whom it pleased me.
27.6: But now I have given all these landes into the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar the King of Babel my servant, and the beastes of the field have I also given him to serve him.
27.7: And all nations shall serve him, and his sonne, and his sonnes sonne until the very time of his land come also: then many nations and great Kinges shall serve themselves of him.
27.8: And the nation and kingdom which will not serve the same Nebuchad-nezzar king of Babel, and that will not put their neck under the yoke of the King of Babel, the same nation will I visit, saith the Lord, with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have wholy given them into his hands.
27.9: Therefore hear not your prophets nor your southsayers, nor your dreamers, nor your inchanters, nor your sorcerers, which say unto you thus, Ye shall not serve the King of Babel.
27.10: For they prophecie a lie unto you to cause you to goe far from your land, and that I should cast you out, and you should perish.
27.11: But the nation that put their neckes under the yoke of the King of Babel, and serve him, those wil I let remain stil in their own land, saith the Lord, and they shall occupie it, and dwel therein.
27.12: I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these wordes, saying, Put your neckes under the yoke of the King of Babel, and serve him and his people, that ye may live.
27.13: Why will ye dye, thou, and thy people by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as the Lord hath spoken against the nation, that will not serve the King of Babel?
27.14: Therefore hear not the words of the prophets, that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the King of Babel: for they prophecie a lie unto you.
27.15: For I have not sent them, saith the Lord, yet they prophecie a lie in my name, that I might cast you out, and that ye might perish, both you, and the prophets that prophecie unto you.
27.16: Also I spake to the Priests, and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hear not the wordes of your prophets that prophecie unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the house of the Lord shall now shortly be brought again from Babel, for they prophecie a lie unto you.
27.17: Hear them not, but serve the King of Babel, that ye may live: wherefore should this citie be desolate?
27.18: But if they be Prophets, and if the word of the Lord be with them, let them intreat the Lord of hostes, that the vessels, which are left in the House of the Lord, and in the house of the King of Judah, and at Jerusalem, go not to Babel.
27.19: For thus saith the Lord of hostes, concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this citie,
27.20: Which Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel took not, when he caryed away captive Jeconiah the sonne of Jehoiakim King of Judah from Jerusalem to Babel, with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
27.21: For thus saith the Lord of hostes the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that remain in the House of the Lord, and in the house of the King of Judah, and at Jerusalem,
27.22: They shall be brought to Babel, and there they shalbe until the day that I visit them, saith the Lord: then will I bring them up, and restore them unto this place.

28.1: And that same yeere in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah King of Judah in the fourth yeere, and in the fifth moneth Hananiah the sonne of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon, spake to mee in the House of the Lord in the presence of the Priestes, and of all the people, and said,
28.2: Thus speaketh the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of the King of Babel.
28.3: Within two yeeres space I will bring into this place all the vessels of the Lords House, that Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel took away from this place, and caried them into Babel.
28.4: And I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the sonne of Jehoiakim King of Judah, with all them that were caried away captive of Judah, and went into Babel, saith the Lord: for I will break the yoke of the King of Babel.
28.5: Then the Prophet Jeremiah said unto the Prophet Hananiah in the presence of ye Priests, and in the presence of all the people that stood in the House of the Lord.
28.6: Even the Prophet Jeremiah sayde, So bee it: the Lord so doe, the Lord confirm thy words which thou hast prophecied to restore the vessels of the Lordes House, and al that is caried captive, from Babel, into this place.
28.7: But hear thou now this word that I will speak in thine eares and in the eares of all the people.
28.8: The Prophets that have been before mee and before thee in time past, prophecied against many countreyes, and against great kingdomes, of war, and of plagues, and of pestilence.
28.9: And the Prophet which prophecieth of peace, when the word of the Prophet shall come to pass, then shall the Prophet be knowen that the Lord hath truely sent him.
28.10: Then Hananiah the Prophet took the yoke from the Prophet Ieremiahs neck, and brake it.
28.11: And Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel, from the neck of al nations within the space of two yeres: and the Prophet Jeremiah went his way.
28.12: Then the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the Prophet, (after that Hananiah the Prophet had broken the yoke from the neck of the Prophet Jeremiah) saying,
28.13: Go, and tell Hananiah, saying, Thus sayth the Lord, Thou hast broken the yokes of wood, but thou shalt make for them yokes of yron.
28.14: For thus saith the Lord of hostes the God of Israel, I have put a yoke of yron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel: for they shall serve him, and I have given him the beasts of the field also.
28.15: Then sayd the Prophet Jeremiah unto the Prophet Hananiah, Hear now Hananiah, the Lord hath not sent thee, but thou makest this people to trust in a lye.
28.16: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will cast thee from of the earth: this yeere thou shalt die, because thou hast spoken rebelliously against the Lord.
28.17: So Hananiah the Prophet died the same yeere in the seventh moneth.

29.1: Now these are the wordes of the book that Jeremiah the Prophet sent from Jerusalem unto the residue of the Elders which were caryed away captives, and to the Priestes, and to the Prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchad-nezzar had caried away captive from Jerusalem to Babel:
29.2: (After that Jeconiah the King, and the Queen, and the eunuches, the princes of Judah, and of Jerusalem, and the workemen, and cunning men were departed from Jerusalem)
29.3: By the hand of Elasah the sonne of Shaphan and Gemariah the sonne of Hilkiah, (whom Zedekiah King of Judah sent unto Babel to Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel) saying,
29.4: Thus hath the Lord of hostes the God of Israel spoken unto all that are caryed away captives, whom I have caused to be caryed away captives from Jerusalem unto Babel:
29.5: Buylde you houses to dwell in, and plant you gardens, and eat the fruites of them.
29.6: Take you wives, and beget sonnes and daughters, and take wives for your sonnes, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sonnes and daughters, that ye may bee increased there, and not diminished.
29.7: And seek the prosperitie of the citie, whither I have caused you to be caried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall you have peace.
29.8: For thus saith the Lord of hostes the God of Israel, Let not your prophets, and your southsayers that bee among you, deceive you, neither give ear to your dreames, which you dream.
29.9: For they prophecie you a lie in my Name: I have not sent them, saith the Lord.
29.10: But thus saith the Lord, That after seuentie yeeres be accomplished at Babel, I will visit you, and perform my good promise toward you, and cause you to return to this place.
29.11: For I know the thoughtes, that I have thought towards you, saith the Lord, even the thoughtes of peace, and not of trouble, to give you an end, and your hope.
29.12: Then shall you crie unto mee, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hear you,
29.13: And ye shall seek mee and find mee, because ye shall seek mee with all your heart.
29.14: And I wil be found of you, saith the Lord, and I will turn away your captiuitie, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places, whither I have cast you, saith the Lord, and will bring you again unto the place, whence I caused you to be caryed away captive.
29.15: Because ye have sayd, The Lord hath raised us up Prophets in Babel,
29.16: Therefore thus saith the Lord of the King, that sitteth upon the throne of David, and of all the people, that dwell in this citie, your brethren that are not gone forth with you into captiuitie:
29.17: Even thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Behold, I will send upon them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like vile figges, that cannot bee eaten, they are so naughtie.
29.18: And I will persecute them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence: and I will make them a terror to all kingdomes of the earth, and a curse, and astonishment and an hissing, and a reproche among all the nations whither I have cast them,
29.19: Because they have not heard my words, saith the Lord, which I sent unto them by my seruantes the Prophetes, rising up earely, and sending them, but yee would not hear, saith the Lord.
29.20: Hear ye therefore the word of the Lord all ye of the captiuitie, whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babel.
29.21: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, of Ahab the sonne of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the sonne of Maaseiah, which prophecie lyes unto you in my Name, Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel, and he shall slay them before your eyes.
29.22: And al they of the captiuitie of Judah, that are in Babel, shall take up this curse against them, and say, The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the King of Babel burnt in the fire,
29.23: Because they have committed vilenie in Israel, and have committed adulterie with their neighbours wives, and have spoken lying words in my Name, which I have not commanded them, even I know it, and testifie it, saith the Lord.
29.24: Thou shalt also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, saying,
29.25: Thus speaketh the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy Name unto all the people, that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the sonne of Maaseiah the Priest, and to all the Priests, saying,
29.26: The Lord hath made thee Priest for Jehoiada the Priest, that yee should bee officers in the House of the Lord, for every man that raueth and maketh himself a Prophet, to put him in prison and in the stockes.
29.27: Now therefore why hast not thou reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which prophecieth unto you?
29.28: For, for this cause hee sent unto us in Babel, saying, This captiuitie is long: buyld houses to dwell in, and plant gardens, and eat the fruites of them.
29.29: And Zephaniah the Priest red this letter in the eares of Jeremiah the Prophet.
29.30: Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,
29.31: Send to all them of the captiuitie, saying, Thus saith the Lord of Shemaiah the Nehelamite, Because that Shemaiah hath prophecied unto you, and I sent him not, and hee caused you to trust in a lye,
29.32: Therefore thus saieth the Lord, Behold, I wil visit Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: hee shall not have a man to dwell among this people, neither shall he behold the good, that I will doe for my people, sayth the Lord, because he hath spoken rebelliously against the Lord.

30.1: The word, that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
30.2: Thus speaketh the Lord God of Israel, saying, Write thee all the wordes, that I have spoken unto thee in a book.
30.3: For loe, the dayes come, saith the Lord, that I wil bring again the captiuitie of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord: for I will restore them unto the land, that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.
30.4: Again, these are the wordes that the Lord spake concerning Israel, and concerning Judah.
30.5: For thus saith the Lord, wee have heard a terrible voyce, of fear and not of peace.
30.6: Demand now and behold, if man trauayle with child? wherefore doe I behold every man with his hands on his loynes as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into a paleness?
30.7: Alas, for this day is great: none hath been like it: it is even the time of Iaakobs trouble, yet shall he be delivered from it.
30.8: For in that day, sayth the Lord of hostes, I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and break thy bondes, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him.
30.9: But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their King, whom I will raise up unto them.
30.10: Therefore fear not, O my servant Iaakob, saith the Lord, neither be afrayde, O Israel: for loe, I will deliver thee from a far countrey, and thy seed from the land of their captiuitie, and Iaakob shall turn again, and shalbe in rest and prosperitie and none shall make him afraid.
30.11: For I am with thee, sayth the Lord, to save thee: though I utterly destroy all the nations where I have scattered thee, yet will I not utterly destroy thee, but I will correct thee by iudgement, and not utterly cut thee off.
30.12: For thus saith the Lord, Thy bruising is incurable, and thy wound is dolorous.
30.13: There is none to judge thy cause, or to lay a plaister: there are no medicines, nor help for thee.
30.14: All thy lovers have forgotten thee: they seek thee not: for I have striken thee with the wound of an enemie, and with a sharp chastisement for ye multitude of thine iniquities, because thy sinnes were increased.
30.15: Why cryest thou for thine affliction? thy sorowe is incurable, for the multitude of thine iniquities: because thy sinnes were increased, I have done these things unto thee.
30.16: Therefore all they that deuoure thee, shall be deuoured, and all thine enemies every one shall goe into captiuitie: and they that spoyle thee, shalbe spoyled, and all they that rob thee, wil I give to be robbed.
30.17: For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy woundes, saith the Lord, because they called thee, The cast away, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.
30.18: Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will bring again the captiuitie of Iaakobs tentes, and have compassion on his dwelling places: and the citie shalbe builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the maner thereof.
30.19: And out of them shall proceed thankesgiuing, and the voyce of them that are joyous, and I will multiplie them, and they shall not bee few: I will also glorifie them, and they shall not be diminished.
30.20: Their children also shall be as afore time, and their congregation shall be established before me: and I will visit all that vex them.
30.21: And their noble ruler shall be of themselves, and their gouernour shall proceed from the middes of them, and I will cause him to draw neere, and approche unto me: for who is this that directeth his heart to come unto mee, saith the Lord?
30.22: And ye shall be my people, and I will bee your God.
30.23: Behold, the tempest of the Lord goeth foorth with wrath: the whirlewinde that hangeth over, shall light upon the head of the wicked.
30.24: The fierce wrath of the Lord shall not return, until he have done, and until he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter dayes ye shall understand it.

31.1: At the same time, saith the Lord, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.
31.2: Thus saith the Lord, The people which escaped the sword, found grace in the wildernes: he walked before Israel to cause him to rest.
31.3: The Lord hath appeared unto me of old, say they: Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love, therefore with mercie I have drawen thee.
31.4: Again I will build thee, and thou shalt be builded, O virgin Israel: thou shalt stil be adorned with thy timbrels, and shalt goe foorth in the dance of them that be ioyfull.
31.5: Thou shalt yet plant vines upon the mountaines of Samaria, and the planters that plant them, shall make them common.
31.6: For the dayes shall come that the watchmen upon the mount of Ephraim shall cry, Arise, and let us go up unto Zion to the Lord our God.
31.7: For thus saith the Lord, Reioyce with gladness for Iaakob, and shout for ioye among the chief of the Gentiles: publish praise, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.
31.8: Behold, I will bring them from the North countrey, and gather them from the coastes of the world, with the blind and the lame among them, with the woman with child, and her that is delivered also: a great companie shall return hither.
31.9: They shall come weeping, and with mercie will I bring them again: I will lead them by the rivers of water in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my first borne.
31.10: Hear the word of the Lord, O ye Gentiles, and declare in the yles afarre off, and say, Hee that scattered Israel, wil gather him and wil keep him, as a shepheard doeth his flock.
31.11: For the Lord hath redeemed Iaakob, and ransomed him from the hand of him, that was stronger then he.
31.12: Therefore they shall come, and reioyce in the height of Zion, and shall runne to the bountifulnes of the Lord, even for the wheat and for the wine, and for the oyle, and for the increase of sheep, and bullocks: and their soul shalbe as a watered garden, and they shall have no more sorow.
31.13: Then shall ye virgin reioyce in the dance, and the yong men and the old men together: for I wil turn their mourning into joy, and wil comfort them, and give them joy for their sorowes.
31.14: And I wil replenish the soul of the Priests with fatness, and my people shalbe satisfied with my goodness, saith the Lord.
31.15: Thus saith the Lord, A voyce was heard on hie, a mourning and bitter weeping. Rahel weeping for her children, refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not.
31.16: Thus saith the Lord, Refrain thy voyce from weeping, and thine eyes from teares: for thy work shalbe rewarded, saith the Lord, and they shall come again from the land of the enemie:
31.17: And there is hope in thine end, saith the Lord, that thy children shall come again to their own borders.
31.18: I have heard Ephraim lamenting thus, Thou hast corrected me, and I was chastised as an vntamed calf: convert thou me, and I shalbe converted: for thou art the Lord my God.
31.19: Surely after that I converted, I repented: and after that I was instructed, I smote upon my thigh: I was ashamed, yea, even confounded, because I did bear the reproch of my youth.
31.20: Is Ephraim my dear sonne or pleasant child? yet since I spake unto him, I still remembred him: therefore my bowels are troubled for him: I wil surely have compassion upon him, saith the Lord.
31.21: Set thee up signes: make thee heapes: set thine heart toward the path and way, that thou hast walked: turn again, O virgin of Israel: turn again to these thy cities.
31.22: How long wilt thou goe astray, O thou rebellious daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth: A WOMAN shall compass a man.
31.23: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Yet shall they say this thing in the land of Judah, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring again their captiuitie, The Lord bless thee, O habitation of justice and holy mountain.
31.24: And Judah shall dwell in it, and all the cities thereof together, the husbandmen and they that goe foorth with the flock.
31.25: For I have saciate the wearie soul, and I have replenished every sorowfull soul.
31.26: Therefore I awaked and beheld, and my sleep was sweet unto me.
31.27: Behold, the dayes come, saith the Lord, that I will sow the house of Israel, and the house of Judah with the seed of man and with the seed of beast.
31.28: And like as I have watched upon them, to pluck up and to root out, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to plague them, so wil I watch over them, to build and to plant them, saith ye Lord.
31.29: In those dayes shall they say no more, The fathers have eaten a sowre grape, and the childrens teeth are set on edge.
31.30: But every one shall die for his own iniquitie: every man that eateth the sowre grape, his teeth shalbe set on edge.
31.31: Behold, the dayes come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah,
31.32: Not according to ye covenant that I made with their fathers, when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, the which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the Lord.
31.33: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel, After those dayes, saith the Lord, I will put my Law in their inward partes, and write it in their hearts, and wil be their God, and they shalbe my people.
31.34: And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord: for I wil forgive their iniquitie, and will remember their sinnes no more.
31.35: Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sunne for a light to the day, and the courses of the moon and of the starres for a light to the night, which breaketh the sea, when the waves thereof roar: his Name is the Lord of hostes.
31.36: If these ordinances depart out of my sight, saith the Lord, then shall the seed of Israel cease from being a nation before me, for ever.
31.37: Thus saith the Lord, If the heavens can be measured, or the fundations of the earth be searched out beneath, then wil I cast off all the seed of Israel, for all that they have done, saith the Lord.
31.38: Behold, the dayes come, saith the Lord, that the citie shalbe built to the Lord from the tower of Hananeel, unto the gate of the corner.
31.39: And the line of the measure shall go foorth in his presence upon the hil Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath.
31.40: And the whole valley of the dead bodies, and of the ashes, and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, and unto the corner of the horsegate toward the East, shalbe holy unto the Lord, neither shall it be plucked up nor destroyed any more for ever.

32.1: The word that came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, in the tenth yere of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eightenth yeere of Nebuchad-nezzar.
32.2: For then the King of Babels host besieged Jerusalem: And Jeremiah the Prophet was shutte up in the court of the prison, which was in the King of Iudahs house.
32.3: For Zedekiah King of Judah had shut him up, saying, Wherefore doest thou prophesie, and say, Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will give this citie into the handes of the King of Babel, and he shall take it?
32.4: And Zedekiah the King of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Caldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the handes of the King of Babel, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his face,
32.5: And he shall lead Zedekiah to Babel, and there shall he be, until I visit him, saith ye Lord: though ye fight with the Caldeans, ye shall not prosper.
32.6: And Jeremiah said, The word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
32.7: Behold, Hanameel, the sonne of Shallum thine uncle, shall come unto thee and say, Bye unto thee my field, that is in Anathoth: for the title by kindred appertaineth unto thee to bye it.
32.8: So Hanameel, mine vncles sonne, came to mee in the court of the prison, according to the word of the Lord, and said unto me, Bye my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the countrey of Beniamin: for the right of the possession is thine, and the purchase belongeth unto thee: bye it for thee. Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
32.9: And I bought the field of Hanameel, mine vncles sonne, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the silver, even seven shekels, and tenne pieces of silver.
32.10: And I writ it in the book and signed it, and took witnesses, and weighed him the silver in the balances.
32.11: So I took the book of the possession, being sealed according to the Law, and custom, with the book that was open,
32.12: And I gave the book of the possession unto Baruch the sonne of Neriah, the sonne of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine vncles sonne, and in the presence of the witnesses, written in the book of the possession, before al the Iewes that sat in the court of the prison.
32.13: And I charged Baruch before them, saying,
32.14: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Take the writings, even this book of the possession, both that is sealed, and this book that is open, and put them in an earthen vessell, that they may continue a long time.
32.15: For the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel saith thus, Houses and fieldes, and vineyardes shall be possessed again in this land.
32.16: Now when I had delivered the book of the possession unto Baruch, the sonne of Neriah, I prayed unto the Lord, saying,
32.17: Ah Lord God, behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power, and by thy stretched out arm, and there is nothing hard unto thee.
32.18: Thou shewest mercie unto thousands, and recompensest the iniquitie of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: O God the great and mightie, whose Name is ye Lord of hostes,
32.19: Great in counsel, and mightie in work, (for thine eyes are open upon all the wayes of ye sonnes of men, to give to every one according to his wayes, and according to the fruit of his workes)
32.20: Which hast set signes and wonders in the land of Egypt unto this day, and in Israel, and among all men, and hast made thee a Name, as appeareth this day,
32.21: And hast brought thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signes, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, with a stretched out arm, and with great terrour,
32.22: And hast given them this land, which thou diddest swear to their fathers to give them, even a land, that floweth with milk and hony,
32.23: And they came in, and possessed it, but they obeyed not thy voyce, neither walked in thy Law: all that thou commaundedst them to doe, they have not done: therefore thou hast caused this whole plague to come upon them.
32.24: Behold, the mounts, they are come into the citie to take it, and the citie is given into the hand of the Caldeans, that fight against it by meanes of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence, and what thou hast spoken, is come to pass, and behold, thou seest it.
32.25: And thou hast sayd unto me, O Lord God, Bye unto thee the field for silver, and take witnesses: for the citie shall be given into the hand of the Caldeans.
32.26: Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,
32.27: Behold, I am the LORD GOD of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
32.28: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Behold, I wil give this citie into the hand of the Caldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchad-nezzar, King of Babel, and he shall take it.
32.29: And the Caldeans shall come and fight against this citie, and set fire on this citie and burn it, with the houses, upon whose rouses they have offred incense unto Baal, and powred drink offrings unto other gods, to provoke me unto anger.
32.30: For the children of Israel, and the children of Judah have surely done evil before me from their youth: for the children of Israel have surely provoked me to anger with the workes of their hands, saith the Lord.
32.31: Therefore this citie hath been unto me as a provocation of mine anger, and of my wrath, from the day, that they built it, even unto this day, that I should remove it out of my sight,
32.32: Because of all the evil of the children of Israel, and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke mee to anger, even they, their Kings, their Princes, their Priests, and their Prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
32.33: And they have turned unto me the back and not the face: though I taught them rising up earely, and instructing them, yet they were not obedient to receive doctrine,
32.34: But they set their abominations in ye house (whereupon my Name was called) to defile it,
32.35: And they built the hie places of Baal, which are in the valley of Ben-hinnom, to cause their sonnes and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech, which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should doe such abomination, to cause Judah to sinne.
32.36: And now therefore, thus hath the Lord God of Israel spoken, concerning this citie, whereof ye say, It shalbe delivered into the hand of the King of Babel by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence,
32.37: Behold, I will gather them out of all countreys, wherein I have scattered them in mine anger, and in my wrath, and in great indignation, and I wil bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely.
32.38: And they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
32.39: And I wil give them one heart and one way that they may fear me for ever for ye wealth of them, and of their children after them.
32.40: And I wil make an everlasting covenant with them, that I wil never turn away from them to doe them good, but I wil put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me.
32.41: Yea, I wil delite in them to do them good, and I wil plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart, and with all my soul.
32.42: For thus sayth the Lord, Like as I have brought all this great plague upon this people, so wil I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
32.43: And the fields shalbe possessed in this land, whereof ye say, It is desolate without man or beast, and shalbe given into the hand of the Caldeans.
32.44: Men shall buy fields for silver, and make writings and seal them, and take witnesses in the land of Beniamin, and round about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountaines, and in the cities of the plain, and in the cities of the South: for I wil cause their captiuitie to return, saith the Lord.

33.1: Moreover, the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the second time (while he was yet shut up in the court of prison) saying,
33.2: Thus sayth the Lord, the maker thereof, the Lord that formed it, and established it, the Lord is his Name.
33.3: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mightie things, which thou knowest not.
33.4: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, concerning the houses of this citie, and concerning the houses of the Kings of Judah, which are destroyed by the mounts, and by the sword,
33.5: They come to fight with the Caldeans, but it is to fill themselves with the dead bodies of men, whom I have slain in mine anger and in my wrath: for I have hid my face from this citie, because of all their wickednes.
33.6: Behold, I will give it health and amendment: for I wil cure them, and will reueile unto them the abundance of peace, and trueth.
33.7: And I wil cause the captiuitie of Judah and the captiuitie of Israel to return, and will build them as at the first.
33.8: And I wil clense them from all their iniquitie, whereby they have sinned against me: yea, I wil pardon all their iniquities, whereby they have sinned against me, and whereby they have rebelled against me.
33.9: And it shalbe to me a name, a joy, a praise, and an honour before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all ye good that I doe unto them: and they shall fear and tremble for all the goodnes, and for all the wealth, that I shew unto this citie.
33.10: Thus sayth the Lord, Again there shalbe heard in this place (which ye say shalbe desolate, without man, and without beast, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streetes of Jerusalem, that are desolate without man, and without inhabitant, and without beast)
33.11: The voyce of joy and the voyce of gladnes, the voyce of the bridegrome, and the voyce of the bride, the voyce of them that shall say, Prayse the Lord of hostes, because the Lord is good: for his mercy endureth for ever, and of them that offer the sacrifice of prayse in the House of the Lord, for I will cause to return the captiuitie of the land, as at the first, sayth the Lord.
33.12: Thus sayth the Lord of hostes, Again in this place, which is desolate, without man, and without beast, and in all the cities thereof there shall be dwelling for shepheards to rest their flockes.
33.13: In the cities of the mountaines, in the cities in the plain, and in the cities of the South, and in the land of Beniamin, and about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah shall the sheep pass again, under the hand of him that telleth them, sayth the Lord.
33.14: Behold, the dayes come, sayth the Lord, that I wil perform that good thing, which I have promised unto the house of Israel, and to the house of Judah.
33.15: In those dayes and at that time, wil I cause the branch of righteousness to grow up unto David, and he shall execute iudgement, and righteousnes in the land.
33.16: In those dayes shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely, and hee that shall call her, is the Lord our righteousness.
33.17: For thus sayth the Lord, David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel.
33.18: Neither shall the Priests and Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to offer meat offerings, and to doe sacrifice continually.
33.19: And the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah, saying,
33.20: Thus sayth the Lord, If you can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, that there should not be day, and night in their season,
33.21: Then may my covenant be broken with David my servant, that he should not have a sonne to reign upon his throne, and with the Levites, and Priests my ministers.
33.22: As the army of heaven can not be nombred, neither the sand of the sea measured: so wil I multiplie the seed of David my servant, and the Levites, that minister unto me.
33.23: Moreover, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
33.24: Considerest thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families, which the Lord hath chosen, hee hath even cast them off? thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them.
33.25: Thus sayth the Lord, If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the order of heaven and earth,
33.26: Then will I cast away the seed of Iaakob and David my servant, and not take of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob: for I wil cause their captiuitie to return, and have compassion on them.

34.1: The word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord (when Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel, and all his host, and all the kingdomes of the earth, that were under the power of his hand, and all people fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cites thereof) saying,
34.2: Thus sayth the Lord God of Israel, Goe, and speak to Zedekiah King of Judah, and tell him, Thus sayth the Lord, Behold, I will give this citie into the hand of the King of Babel, and he shall burn it with fire,
34.3: And thou shall not escape out of his hand, but shalt surely be taken, and delivered into his hand, and thine eyes shall behold the face of the King of Babel, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babel.
34.4: Yet hear the word of the Lord, O Zedekiah, King of Judah: thus sayth the Lord of thee, Thou shalt not dye by the sword,
34.5: But thou shalt die in peace: and according to the burning for thy fathers the former Kings which were before thee, so shall they burn odours for thee, and they shall lament thee, saying, Oh lord: for I have pronounced the word, sayth the Lord.
34.6: Then Jeremiah the Prophet spake all these words unto Zedekiah King of Judah in Jerusalem,
34.7: (When the King of Babels host fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah, that were left, even against Lachish, and against Azekah: for these strong cities remained of the cities of Judah)
34.8: This is the word that came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, after that the King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people, which were at Jerusalem, to proclaim libertie unto them,
34.9: That every man should let his servant go free, and every man his handmayde, which was an Ebrue or an Ebruesse, and that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Iewe his brother.
34.10: Now when all the princes, and all the people which had agreed to the covenant, heard that every one should let his servant go free, and every one his handmaid, and that none should serve them selves of them any more, they obeyed and let them go.
34.11: But afterward they repented and caused the servants and the handmayds, whom they had let go free, to return, and held them in subiection as servants and handmayds.
34.12: Therefore the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
34.13: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I made a covenant with your fathers, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of servants, saying,
34.14: At the terme of seven yeres let ye go, every man his brother an Ebrewe which hath been sold unto thee: and when he hath served the six yeres, thou shalt let him go free from thee: but your fathers obeyed me not, neither inclined their eares.
34.15: And ye were now turned, and had done right in my sight in proclayming libertie, every man to his neighbour, and ye had made a covenant before mee in the house, whereupon my Name is called.
34.16: But ye repented, and polluted my Name: for ye have caused every man his servant, and every man his handmayde, whom ye had set at libertie at their pleasure, to return, and hold them in subiection to bee unto you as seruantes and as handmaydes.
34.17: Therefore thus saith the Lord, Ye have not obeyed mee, in proclayming freedom every man to his brother, and every man to his neighbour: behold, I proclaim a libertie for you, saith the Lord, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine, and I will make you a terrour to all the kingdomes of the earth.
34.18: And I will give those men that have broken my covenant, and have not kept the wordes of the covenant, which they had made before me, when they cut the calf in twain, and passed between the partes thereof:
34.19: The princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the Eunuches, and the Priestes, and all the people of the land, which passed between the partes of the calf,
34.20: I wil even give them into the hand of their enemies, and into the handes of them that seek their life: and their dead bodies shalbe for meat unto the foules of the heaven, and to the beastes of the earth.
34.21: And Zedekiah King of Judah, and his princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the King of Babels host, which are gone up from you.
34.22: Behold, I will command, saith the Lord, and cause them to return to this citie, and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it with fire: and I will make the cities of Judah desolate without an inhabitant.

35.1: The word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, in the dayes of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, saying,
35.2: Go unto the house of the Rechabites, and speak unto them, and bring them into the house of the Lord into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
35.3: Then took I Jaazaniah, the sonne of Jeremiah the sonne of Habazziniah, and his brethren, and all his sonnes, and the whole house of the Rechabites,
35.4: And I brought them into the House of the Lord, into the chamber of the sonnes of Hanan, the sonne of Igdaliah a man of God, which was by the chamber of the princes, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the sonne of Shallum, the keeper of the treasure.
35.5: And I set before the sonnes of the house of the Rechabites, pots full of wine, and cuppes, and said unto them, Drink wine.
35.6: But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the sonne of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither you nor your sonnes for ever.
35.7: Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any, but all your dayes ye shall dwell in tentes, that ye may live a long time in the land where ye be strangers.
35.8: Thus have wee obeyed the voyce of Jonadab the sonne of Rechab our father, in all that he hath charged us, and wee drink no wine all our dayes, neither wee, our wives, our sonnes, nor our daughters.
35.9: Neither build wee houses for us to dwell in, neither have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed,
35.10: But we have remained in tentes, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
35.11: But when Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel came up into the land, we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem, from the host of the Caldeans, and from the host of Aram: so we dwel at Jerusalem.
35.12: Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,
35.13: Thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Goe, and tell the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will ye not receive doctrine to obey my wordes, saith the Lord?
35.14: The commandement of Jonadab the sonne of Rechab that hee commanded his sonnes, that they should drink no wine, is surely kept: for unto this day they drink none, but obey their fathers commandement: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising earely, and speaking, but ye would not obey me.
35.15: I have sent also unto you all my servants the Prophetes, rising up earely, and sending, them, saying, Return now every man from his evil way, and amend your workes, and goe not after other gods to serve them, and ye shall dwel in the land which I have given unto you, and to your fathers, but ye would not encline your ear, nor obey mee.
35.16: Surely the sonnes of Jonadab the sonne of Rechab, have kept the commandement of their father, which he gave them, but this people hath not obeyed me.
35.17: Therefore thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Behold, I will bring upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, all the evil that I have pronounced against them, because I have spoke unto them, but they would not hear, and I have called unto them, but they would not answer.
35.18: And Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, Thus saith the Lord of hostes the God of Israel, Because ye have obeyed the commandement of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that hee hath commanded you,
35.19: Therefore thus saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Jonadab the sonne of Rechab shall not want a man, to stand before me for ever.

36.1: And in the fourth yeere of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, came this word unto Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
36.2: Take thee a roule or book, and write therein all the wordes that I have spoken to thee against Israel, and against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day that I spake unto thee, even from the dayes of Josiah unto this day.
36.3: It may bee that the House of Judah will hear of all the evil, which I determined to doe unto them that they may return every man from his evil way, that I may forgive their iniquitie and their sinnes.
36.4: Then Jeremiah called Baruch the sonne of Neriah, and Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah all the wordes of the Lord, which hee had spoken unto him, upon a roule or book.
36.5: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up, and can not go into the House of the Lord.
36.6: Therefore goe thou, and read the roule wherein thou hast written at my mouth the words of the Lord in the audience of the people in the Lordes House upon the fasting day: also thou shalt read them in the hearing of all Judah, that come out of their cities.
36.7: It may be that they will pray before the Lord, and every one return from his evil way, for great is the anger and the wrath, that the Lord hath declared against this people.
36.8: So Baruch the sonne of Neriah did according unto all, that Jeremiah the Prophet commanded him, reading in the book the wordes of the Lord in the Lords House.
36.9: And in the fift yeere of Jehoiakim the sonne of Josiah King of Judah, in the ninth moneth, they proclaimed a fast before the Lord to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all the people that came from the cities of Judah unto Jerusalem.
36.10: Then read Baruch in the book the wordes of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah the sonne of Shaphan the secretarie, in the hier court at the entrie of the new gate of the Lordes house, in the hearing of all the people.
36.11: When Michaiah the sonne of Gemariah, the sonne of Shaphan had heard out of the book all the wordes of the Lord,
36.12: Then hee went down to the Kings house into the Chancellours chamber, and loe, all the princes sat there, even Elishama the Chancellour, and Delaiah the sonne of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the sonne of Achbor, and Gemariah the sonne of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the sonne of Hananiah, and all the princes.
36.13: Then Michaiah declared unto them all the wordes that he had heard when Baruch read in the book in the audience of the people.
36.14: Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the sonne of Nethaniah, the sonne of Shelemiah, the sonne of Chushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roule, wherein thou hast read in the audience of the people, and come. So Baruch the sonne of Neriah, took the roule in his hand, and came unto them.
36.15: And they said unto him, Sit down now, and read it, that we may hear. So Baruch read it in their audience.
36.16: Now when they had heard all the wordes, they were afraid both one and other, and said unto Baruch, We will certifie the King of all these wordes.
36.17: And they examined Baruch, saying, Tell us now, how diddest thou write all these wordes at his mouth?
36.18: Then Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these wordes unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ynke in the book.
36.19: Then said the princes unto Baruch, Goe, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah, and let no man know where ye be.
36.20: And they went in to the King to the court, but they layde up the roule in the chamber of Elishama the Chancellour and told the King all the wordes, that he might hear.
36.21: So the King sent Jehudi to fet the roule, and he took it out of Elishama the Chancellours chamber, and Jehudi read it in the audience of the King, and in the audience of all the princes, which stood beside the King.
36.22: Now the King sat in the winter House, in the ninth moneth, and there was a fire burning before him.
36.23: And when Jehudi had read three, or four sides, hee cut it with the penknife and cast it into the fire, that was on the hearth until all the roule was consumed in the fire, that was on the hearth.
36.24: Yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garmets, neither the King, nor any of his servants, that heard all these wordes.
36.25: Nevertheless, Elnathan, and Delaiah, and Gemariah had besought the King, that he would not burn ye roule: but he would not hear them.
36.26: But the King commanded Jerahmeel the sonne of Hammelech, and Seraiah the sonne of Azriel, and Shelemiah the sonne of Abdiel, to take Baruch the scribe, and Jeremiah the Prophet, but the Lord hid them.
36.27: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah (after that the King had burnt the roule and the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah) saying,
36.28: Take thee again another roule and write in it all ye former words that were in the first roule which Jehoiakim the King of Judah hath burnt,
36.29: And thou shalt say to Jehoiakim King of Judah, Thus saith the Lord, Thou hast burnt this roule, saying, Why hast thou written therein, saying, that the King of Babel shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall take thence both man and beast?
36.30: Therefore thus saith the Lord of Jehoiakim King of Judah, Hee shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.
36.31: And I will visit him and his seed, and his servants for their iniquitie, and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah all the evil that I have pronounced against them: but they would not hear.
36.32: Then took Jeremiah another roule, and gave it Baruch the scribe the sonne of Neriah, which wrote therein at the mouth of Jeremiah all the wordes of the book which Jehoiakim King of Judah had burnt in the fire, and there were added besides them many like wordes.

37.1: And King Zedekiah the sonne of Josiah reigned for Coniah the sonne of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchad-nezzar King of Babel made King in the land of Judah.
37.2: But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land would obey the wordes of the Lord, which he spake by the ministerie of the Prophet Jeremiah.
37.3: And Zedekiah the King sent Jehucal the sonne of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah the sonne of Maaseiah the Priest to the Prophet Jeremiah, saying, Pray now unto the Lord our God for us.
37.4: (Now Jeremiah went in and out among the people: for they had not put him into the prison.
37.5: Then Pharaohs host was come out of Egypt: and when the Caldeans that besieged Jerusalem, heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem)
37.6: Then came the word of the Lord unto the Prophet Jeremiah, saying,
37.7: Thus sayth the Lord God of Israel, Thus shall ye say to the King of Judah, that sent you unto me to inquire of me, Behold, Pharaohs host, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.
37.8: And the Caldeans shall come again, and fight against this citie, and take it and burn it with fire.
37.9: Thus sayth the Lord, Deceive not your selves, saying, The Caldeans shall surely depart from us: for they shall not depart.
37.10: For though ye had smitten the whole host of the Caldeans that fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should every man rise up in his tent, and burn this citie with fire.
37.11: When the host of the Caldeans was broken up from Jerusalem, because of Pharaohs armie,
37.12: Then Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to goe into the land of Beniamin, separating himself thence from among the people.
37.13: And when hee was in the gate of Beniamin, there was a chief officer, whose name was Iriiah, the sonne of Shelemiah, the sonne of Hananiah, and he took Jeremiah the Prophet, saying, Thou fleest to the Caldeans.
37.14: Then sayde Jeremiah, That is false, I flee not to the Caldeans: but he would not hear him: so Iriiah took Jeremiah, and brought him to the princes.
37.15: Wherefore the princes were angry with Jeremiah, and smote him, and layde him in prison in the house of Jehonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison.
37.16: When Jeremiah was entred into the dungeon, and into the prisons, and had remained there a long time,
37.17: Then Zedekiah the King sent, and took him out, and the King asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the Lord? And Jeremiah sayd, Yea: for, sayd he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the King of Babel.
37.18: Moreover, Jeremiah sayd unto King Zedekiah, What have I offended against thee, or against thy servants, or against this people, that ye have put me in prison?
37.19: Where are now your prophets, which prophecied unto you, saying, The King of Babel shall not come against you, nor against this land?
37.20: Therefore hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the King: let my prayer be accepted before thee, that thou cause mee not to return to the house of Jehonathan the scribe, least I die there.
