24:3:1: And I will not cast thee off, but receive thee, according to my mercy.
According as it is written, Deut. 24:4.
If he take such one to wife again.
That is, with idols, and with them whom thou hast put thy confidence in.
24:3:2: Which dwelleth in tents and waiteth for them that pass by to spoil them.
24:3:3: As God threatened by his Law, Deut. 28:24.
Thou wouldest never be ashamed of thine acts and repent: and this impudency is common to idolaters, which will not give off, though they be never so manifestly convicted.
24:3:4: He showeth that the wicked in their miseries will cry unto God and use outward prayer as the godly do, but because they turn not from their evil, they are not heard, Isa. 58:3, 4.
24:3:8: And gave her into the hands of the Assyrians.
24:3:9: The Hebrew word may either signify lightness, and wantonness, or noise and brute.
24:3:10: Judah feigned for a time that she did return, as under Josiah and other good kings, but she was never truly touched, or wholly reformed, as appeared when occasion was offered by any wicked prince.
24:3:11: Israel hath not declared herself so wicked as Judah, which yet hath had more admonitions and examples to call her to repentance.
24:3:12: Whereas the Israelites were now kept in captivity by the Assyrians, to whom he promiseth mercy, if they will repent.
24:3:13: There was no way, which thou didst not haunt to seek after the idols, and to trot a pilgrimage.
24:3:16: This is to be understood of the coming of Christ: for then they shall not seek the Lord by ceremonies, and all figures shall cease.
24:3:17: Meaning, the Church, where the Lord will be present to the world’s end, Matt. 28:20.
24:3:18: Where they are now in captivity.
24:3:20: The Hebrew word signifieth a friend or companion, and here may be taken for a husband, as it is used also, Hos. 3:1.
24:3:21: Signifying, that God, whom they had forsaken, would bring their enemies unto them, who should lead them captive, and make them to cry and lament.
24:3:22: This is spoken in the person of Israel to the shame of Judah, which stayed so long to turn unto God.
24:3:24: For their idolatry God’s vengeance hath light upon them and theirs.
24:3:25: They justify not themselves, or say that they would follow their fathers, but condemn their wicked doings and desire forgiveness of the same, as Ezra 9:7; Ps. 106:6; Isa. 64:6.
24:4:1: That is, wholly, and without hypocrisy, Joel 2:12, not dissembling to turn and serve God as they do which serve him by halves, as Hos. 7:16.
24:4:2: Thou shalt detest the name of idols, Ps. 16:4, and shalt with reverence swear by the living God, when thine oath may advance God’s glory, and profit others: and here, by swearing he meaneth the true religion of God.
24:4:4: He willeth them to pluck up the impiety and wicked affection and worldly respects out of their heart, that the true seed of God’s word may be sown therein, Hos. 10:12, and this is the true circumcision of the heart, Deut. 10:16; Rom. 2:29; Col. 2:11.
24:4:5: He warneth them of the great dangers that shall come upon them by the Chaldeans, except, they repent and turn to the Lord.
24:4:6: He speaketh this to admonish them of the great danger when every man shall prepare to save himself, but it shall be too late, 2 Kings 25:4.
24:4:7: Meaning, Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon, 2 Kings 24:1.
24:4:9: That is, the false prophets, which still prophesied peace and security.
24:4:10: By the false prophets which promised peace and tranquility: and thus thou hast punished their rebellious stubbornness by causing them to hearken unto lies which would not believe thy truth, 1 Kings 22:23; Ezek. 14:9; 2 Thess. 2:11.
24:4:11: But to carry away both corn, and chaff.
The North wind whereby he meaneth Nebuchadnezzar.
24:4:13: Meaning, that Nebuchadnezzar should come as suddenly, as a cloud that is carried with the wind.
This is spoken in the person of all the people, who in their affliction should cry thus.
24:4:15: Which was in the mid-way between Dan and Jerusalem.
Which was a city in the utmost border of Israel Northward toward Babylon.
24:4:17: Which keep the fruits so straightly, that nothing can come in nor out: so should the Babylonians compass Judah.
24:4:19: He showeth that the true ministers are lively touched with the calamities of the Church, so that all the parts of their body feel the grief of their heart, albeit with zeal to God’s glory they pronounce his judgments against the people.
24:4:20: Meaning, the cities, which were as easily cast down as a tent.
24:4:22: Their wisdom and policy tend to their own destruction and pulleth them from God.
24:4:23: By these manner of speeches he showeth the horrible destruction that should come upon the land, and also condemneth the obstinacy of the people, who repent not at the fear of these terrible tidings, seeing that the insensible creatures are moved therewith, as if the order of nature should be changed, Isa. 13:10 and 24:23; Ezek. 32:7; Joel 2:31 and 3:15.
24:4:27: But for his mercy’s sake, he will reserve himself a residue to be his Church, and to praise him in earth, Isa. 1:9.
24:4:30: Neither thy ceremonies nor rich gifts shall deliver thee.
24:4:31: As the Prophets were moved to pity the destruction of their people, so they declared it to the people to move them to repentance, Isa. 22:4; Jer. 9:1.
24:5:2: Though they pretend religion and holiness, yet all is but hypocrisy: for under this kind of swearing is contained the true religion.
24:5:3: Dost not thou love uprightness and faithful dealing?
Thou hast ofttimes punished them, but all is in vain, Isa. 9:13.
24:5:5: He speaketh this to the reproach of them which should govern and teach others, and yet are farther out of the way than the simple people.
24:5:7: He showeth that to swear by anything than by God, is to forsake him.
24:5:10: He commandeth the Babylonians and enemies to destroy them.
24:5:12: Because they gave no credit to the words of his Prophets, as Isa. 28:15.
24:5:13: Their words shall be of none effect, but vain.
They are not sent of the Lord, and therefore that which they threaten to us shall come upon them.
24:5:15: To wit, the Babylonians and Chaldeans.
24:5:16: Who shall kill many with their arrows.
24:5:18: Here the Lord declareth his unspeakable favor toward his Church, as Jer. 4:27.
24:5:25: If there be any stay, that we receive not God’s blessings in abundance, we must consider that it is for our own iniquities, Isa. 59:1, 2.
24:5:28: They feel not the plague of God for it.
24:5:31: Meaning that there could be nothing but disorder, where the ministers were wicked persons and corrupt.
24:6:1: Which was a city in Judah, six miles from Bethlehem, 2 Chron. 11:6.
He speaketh to them chiefly because they should take heed by the example of their brethren, the other half of their tribe, which were now carried away prisoners.
24:6:2: I have entreated her gently, and given her abundance of all things.
24:6:3: She shall be so destroyed; that the sheep may be fed in her.
24:6:4: He speaketh this in the person of the Babylonians, which complain that the time faileth them before they have brought their enterprises to pass.
24:6:7: He showeth the cause why it should be destroyed, and how it cometh of themselves.
24:6:8: He warneth them to amend by his correction, and turn to him by repentance.
24:6:9: He exhorteth the Babylonians to be diligent to search out all and to leave none.
24:6:10: They delight to hear vain things, and to shut up their ears to true doctrine.
24:6:11: As the Lord had given him his word to be as a fire of his indignation to burn the wicked, Jer. 5:14, so he kindleth it now when he seeth that all remedies are past.
24:6:14: When the people began to fear God’s judgments, the false prophets comforted them by flatterings, showing that God would send peace and not war.
24:6:16: Wherein the Patriarchs and Prophets walked, directed by the word of God: signifying that there is no true way, but that which God prescribeth.
24:6:17: Prophets which should warn you of the dangers that were at hand.
24:6:18: God taketh all the world to witness, and the insensible creatures, of the ingratitude of the Jews.
24:6:22: From Babylon by Dan, which was North from Jerusalem.
24:6:24: For fear of the enemy: he speaketh this in the person of the Jews.
24:6:27: Meaning, Jeremiah, whom God had appointed to try out the godly from the wicked, as a founder doth the pure metal from the dross.
24:6:29: All the pain and labor that hath been taken with them, is lost.
24:7:4: Believe not the false prophets, which say that for the Temple’s sake, and the sacrifices there, the Lord will preserve you, and so nourish you in your sin, and vain confidence.
24:7:7: God showeth on what condition he made his promise to this Temple: that they should be an holy people unto him, as he would be a faithful God to them.
24:7:11: As thieves hid in holes and dens think themselves safe, so when you are in my Temple, you think to be covered with the holiness thereof, and that I cannot see your wickedness, Matt. 21:13.
24:7:12: Because they depended so much on the Temple, which was for his promise, that he would be present and defend them where the Ark was, he sendeth them to God’s judgments against Shiloh, where the Ark had remained about 300 years, and after was taken, the Priests slain, and the people miserably discomfited, 1 Sam. 4:11; Jer. 26:6.
24:7:13: That is, I never ceased to warn you, as Isa. 65:2; Prov. 1:23.
He showeth what is the only remedy to redress our faults: to suffer God to lead us into the way, and to obey his calling, Isa. 66:4.
24:7:15: I will send you into captivity as I have done Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes.
24:7:16: To assure them that God had determined with himself to punish their wickedness, he showeth that the prayer of the godly can nothing avail them, whiles they remain in their obstinacy against God, and will not use the means that he useth to call them to repentance, Jer. 11:14 and 14:11.
24:7:18: That is, they sacrifice to the Sun, Moon and Stars, which they called the queen of heaven, Jer. 44:17; 2 Kings 23:5.
24:7:22: Showing that it was not his chief purpose and intent, that they should offer sacrifices: but that they should regard, wherefore they were ordained: to wit, to be joined to the word as seals and confirmations of remissions of sins in Christ: for without the word they were vain and unprofitable.
24:7:25: Which was about fourteen hundred years.
24:7:27: Whereby he showeth that the pastors ought not to leave their flocks in their obstinacy, for the Lord will use the means of his servants to make the wicked more faulty and to prove his.
24:7:29: In sign of mourning, as Job 1:20.
Against whom he had just occasion to pour out his wrath, Mic. 1:6.
24:7:31: But commanded the contrary, as Lev. 18:21 and 20:3; Deut. 18:10.
24:8:1: The enemy for greediness of gain shall rifle your graves, and lay you before those idols, which in your life you worshipped, to see if they can help you.
24:8:3: Because of the afflictions that they shall feel through God’s judgments.
24:8:4: Is there no hope that they will return?
24:8:6: They are full of hypocrisy, and everyone followeth his own fantasy without any consideration.
24:8:7: He accuseth them in that that they are more ignorant of God’s judgments, than these birds are of their appointed seasons to discern the cold and heat, as Isa. 1:3.
24:8:8: The Law doth not profit you, neither need it to have been written for ought that you have learned by it.
24:8:9: They that seem wise, may be ashamed of their ignorance, for all wisdom consisteth in God’s word.
24:8:14: That is, hath brought us into extreme affliction, and thus they shall not attribute this plague to fortune, but to God’s just judgment, Jer. 9:15 and 23:15.
He speaketh in the person of the people, who when the enemy cometh, will turn about to hide themselves, and acknowledge that it is God’s hand.
24:8:17: God threateneth to send the Babylonians among them, who shall utterly destroy them in such sort, as by no means they shall escape.
24:8:20: The people wonder that they have so long time looked for succor in vain.
24:8:22: Meaning, that no man’s help or means could save them: for in Gilead was precious balm, Jer. 46:11, or else deriding the vain confidence of the people, who looked for help at their Priests, who should have been the Physicians of their souls, and dwelt at Gilead, Hos. 6:8.
24:9:1: The Prophet showeth the great compassion that he had toward this people, seeing that he could never sufficiently lament the destruction that he saw to hang over them, which is a special note to discern the true pastors from the hirelings, read Jer. 4:19.
24:9:2: He showeth that this were more quietness and greater safety for him to dwell among the wild beasts than among this wicked people, save that God hath enjoined him this charge.
24:9:3: To belie and slander their neighbors.
24:9:4: Meaning, that all were corrupt, and none could find an honest man.
24:9:5: They have so practiced deceit, that they cannot forsake it.
24:9:6: They had rather forsake God, than leave their wicked trade.
24:9:10: Signifying, that all the places about Jerusalem should be destroyed.
24:9:12: Meaning, that they are all without sense and understanding, and that God hath taken his spirit from them.
24:9:14: He showeth that the children cannot excuse themselves by their fathers: for both father and child if they be wicked shall perish.
24:9:17: Seeing you cannot lament your own sins, call for those foolish women, whom of a superstition you have to lament for the dead, that they by their feigned tears may provoke you to some sorrow.
24:9:19: As though they were weary of us, because of our iniquities, Lev. 18:28 and 20:22.
24:9:20: He derideth the superstition of the women which made an art of mourning, and taught to weep with feigned tears.
24:9:21: Signifying, that there is no means to deliver the wicked from God’s judgments: but when they think to be most sure, and most far off, then they are soonest taken.
24:9:23: Forasmuch as none can save himself by his own labor, or any worldly means, he showeth that it is vain to put our trust therein, but that we trust in the Lord, and rejoice in him, who only can deliver us, 1 Cor. 1:31; 2 Cor. 10:17.
24:9:24: These three points are necessary to know aright: his mercy, wherein consisteth our salvation, his judgment, which he executeth continually against the wicked, and his justice, whereby he defendeth and maintaineth the faithful.
24:9:25: Meaning, both Jews and Gentiles, as in this next verse he showeth the cause, read Jer. 4:4.
24:10:2: God forbiddeth his people to give credit or fear the constellations and conjunctions of stars and planets which have no power of themselves, but are governed by him, and their secret motions and influences are not known to man and therefore there can be no certain judgment thereof, Deut. 18:9.
24:10:3: Meaning, not only in the observation of the stars, but their laws and ceremonies whereby they confirm their idolatry, which is forbidden, Deut. 12:30.
24:10:4: The Prophets use thus plainly and simply to set forth the vile absurdity of the idolaters, that men might learn to be ashamed of that whereunto their corrupt nature is most subject, read Isa. 44:12.
24:10:6: He teacheth the people to lift up their eyes to God, who hath all power and therefore ought only to be feared: and herein he showeth them not only the evil that they ought to eschew: but the good which they ought to follow, Rev. 15:4.
24:10:8: Because the people thought that to have images, was a means to serve God, and to bring them to the knowledge of him, he showeth that nothing more displeaseth God, nor bringeth man into greater errors and ignorance of God: and therefore he calleth them the doctrine of vanity, the work of errors, verse 15, and Hab. 2:18 calleth them the teachers of lies: contrary to that wicked opinion, that they are the books of the lay people.
24:10:9: Whereas they found the best gold: showing, that they thought nothing too dear for their idols, some read Ophir, as 1 Kings 9:28.
24:10:11: This declareth that all that hath been in this chapter spoken of idols, was to arm the Jews when they should be in Chaldea among the idolaters, and now with one sentence he instructeth them both how to protect their own religion against the idolaters, and how to answer them to their shame which should exhort them to idolatry, and therefore he writeth this sentence in the Chaldean’s tongue for a memorial, whereas all the rest of his writing is Hebrew.
24:10:14: The more that man thinketh to do anything well by his own wisdom, and not as God instructeth him, the more doth he prove himself to be a vile beast.
24:10:16: By these words Portion and Rod, he signifieth their inheritance, meaning, that God should be all sufficient for them: and that their felicity consisted in him alone, and therefore they ought to renounce all other helps and succors as of idols, etc. Deut. 32:9; Ps. 16:5.
24:10:17: The Prophet willeth the Jews to prepare themselves to this captivity, showing that it was now at hand that they should feel the things whereof he had told them.
24:10:19: It is my just plague, and therefore I will take it patiently: whereby he teacheth the people how to behave themselves toward God.
24:10:20: He showeth how Jerusalem shall lament.
24:10:23: He speaketh this because that Nebuchadnezzar purposed to have made war against the Moabites and Ammonites, but hearing of Zedekiah’s rebellion, he turned his power to go against Jerusalem, Ezek. 21:21, therefore the Prophet saith, that this was the Lord’s direction.
24:10:24: Considering that God had revealed unto him the certitude of their captivity, Jer. 7:16, he only prayeth, that he would punish them with mercy, which Isaiah calleth in measure, Isa. 27:8, measuring his rods by their infirmity, 1 Cor. 10:13, for here by judgment is meant not only the punishment, but also the merciful moderation of the same, as Jer. 30:11.
24:10:25: Forasmuch as God cannot only be known and glorified by his mercy, that he useth toward his Church, but also by his justice in punishing his enemies, he prayeth that this glory may fully appear both in the one and the other, Ps. 79:6.
24:11:3: He calleth the Jews to the consideration of God’s mercy, who freely chose them, made a covenant of eternal felicity with them, and how he ever performed it on his behalf, and how they ever showed themselves rebellious and ingrate toward him, and brake it on their part, and so are subject to the curse of the Law, Deut. 27:26.
24:11:5: Thus he speaketh in the person of the people, which agreed to the covenant.
24:11:8: According to his own fantasy, and not as my word appointed him.
Meaning, the menaces and curses contained in the Law, Lev. 26:14; Deut. 28:16.
24:11:9: That is, a general consent to rebel against me.
24:11:11: Because they will not pray with true faith and repentance, but for the smart and grief which they feel, Prov. 1:28.
24:11:15: My people of Israel, whom I have hitherto so greatly loved.
Meaning, that they offer not in the Temple to God, but on the altars of Baal and the idols, and so rejoiced in their wickedness.
24:11:18: Which went about privily to conspire my death.
24:11:19: Let us destroy the Prophet and his doctrine. Some read, Let us corrupt his meat with wood, meaning, poison.
24:11:20: Thus he spake, not for hatred, but being moved with the Spirit of God, he desireth the advancement of God’s glory, and the verifying of his word, which is by the destruction of his enemies.
24:11:21: To wit, both the Priests and the rest of the people: for this town was the Priests, and they dwelt in it, read Jer. 1:1.

Not that they could not abide to hear God named: (for herein they would show themselves most holy) but because they could not abide to be sharply reproved, and therefore desired to be flattered, Isa. 30:10, and to be maintained in their pleasures, Mic. 2:11, and not to hear vice condemned, Amos 7:12.
24:12:1: The Prophet confesseth God to be just in all his doings, although man be not able to give a reason of all his acts.
This question hath been always a great tentation to the godly, to see the wicked enemies of God in prosperity, and his dear children in adversity, as Job 21:7; Ps. 37:1 and 73:3; Hab. 1:3.
24:12:2: They profess God in mouth, but deny him in heart, which is here meant by the reins, Isa. 29:13; Matt. 15:8.
24:12:3: The Hebrew word is, Sanctify them, meaning, that God would be sanctified in the destruction of the wicked, to whom God for a while giveth prosperity, that afterward they should the more feel his heavy judgment when they lack their riches which were a sign of his mercy.
24:12:4: Abusing God’s lenity and his promises, they flattered themselves as though God would ever be merciful, and not utterly destroy them: therefore they hardened themselves in sin, till at length the beasts and insensible creatures felt the punishment of their stubborn rebellion against God.
24:12:5: Some think that God reproveth Jeremiah, in that that he would reason with him, saying, that if he were not able to march with men, that he were far unable to dispute with God. Others, by the footmen, mean them of Anathoth: and by the horsemen, them of Jerusalem, which should trouble the Prophet worse than his own countrymen did.
24:12:7: God willeth the Prophet to denounce his judgments against Jerusalem, notwithstanding that they shall both by threatenings and flatteries, labor to put him to silence.
24:12:8: Ever ramping and raging against me and my Prophets.
24:12:9: Instead of bearing my livery, and wearing only my colors, they have change and diversity of colors of their idols and superstitions, therefore their enemies as thick as the fowls of the air shall come about them to destroy them.
24:12:10: He prophecieth of the destruction of Jerusalem, by the captains of Nebuchadnezzar, whom he calleth pastors.
24:12:11: Because no man regardeth my word, or the plagues that I have sent upon the land.
24:12:13: They lamented the sins of the people.
For instead of amendment, you grew worse and worse, as God’s plagues testified.
24:12:14: Meaning, the wicked enemies of his Church, which blasphemed his Name, and whom he would punish after that he hath delivered his people.
24:12:15: After that I have punished the Gentiles, I will have mercy upon them.
24:12:16: The true doctrine and manner to serve God.
They shall be of the number of the faithful, and have a place in my Church.
24:13:4: Because this river Perath or Euphrates was far from Jerusalem, it is evident that this was a vision, whereby was signified that the Jews should pass over Euphrates to be captives in Babylon, and there for length of time should seem to be rotten, although they were joined to the Lord before as a girdle about a man.
24:13:12: Every one of you shall be filled with spiritual drunkenness, and be without all knowledge to seek how to help yourselves.
24:13:14: It shall be as easy for me to destroy the greatest and the strongest, as it is for a man to break earthen bottles.
24:13:16: That is, affliction and misery by the Babylonians, Isa. 8:22.
Meaning, for help and support of the Egyptians.
24:13:17: You shall surely be led away captive, and I, according to mine affection towards you, shall weep and lament for your stubbornness.
24:13:18: For Jehoiachin and his mother rendered themselves by Jeremiah’s counsel to the king of Babylon, 2 Kings 24:12.
24:13:19: That is, of Judah, which lieth Southward from Babylon.
24:13:20: He asketh the king, where his people is become.
24:13:21: By seeking to strangers for help, thou hast made them skillful to fight against thee.
24:13:22: The cloak of hypocrisy shall be pulled off, and thy shame seen.
24:13:26: As thine iniquities have been manifest to all the world, so shall thy shame and punishment.
24:13:27: He compareth idolaters to horses inflamed after mares.
There is no place so high nor low, whereas the marks and signs of thine idolatry appear not.
24:14:1: Which came for lack of rain, as verse 4.
24:14:2: The word signifieth to be made black, and so is here taken for extreme sorrow.
24:14:3: To wit, with ashes in token of sorrow.
24:14:5: Meaning, that the brute beasts for drought were compelled to forsake their young, contrary to nature, and to go seek water which they could not find.
24:14:6: Which are so hot of nature, that they cannot be cooled with drinking of water, but still gape for the air to resisteth them.
24:14:7: He showeth the only way to remedy to God’s plagues, which is by unfeigned confession of our sins, and returning to him by repentance.
24:14:8: That taketh no care for us.
24:14:9: As one that hath strength to help, and yet is afraid to put to his hand.
24:14:13: He pitieth the people, and accuseth the false prophets, which deceived them: but the Lord answered, that both the prophets, which deceived, and the people, which suffered themselves to be seduced, shall perish, Jer. 23:15 and 27:8, 9 and 29:8.
24:14:17: The false prophets promised peace and assurance, but Jeremiah calleth to tears, and repentance for their affliction, which is at hand, as Jer. 9:1; Lam. 1:16 and 2:18.
24:14:18: Both high and low shall be led captives into Babylon.
24:14:19: Though the Prophet knew that God had cast off the multitude, which were hypocrites, and bastard children, yet he was assured that for his promise sake he would have still a Church, for the which he prayeth.
24:14:20: He teacheth the Church a form of prayer to humble themselves to God by true repentance, which is the only means to avoid this famine, which was the beginning of God’s plagues.
24:15:1: Meaning, that if there were any man living moved with so great zeal toward the people as were these two, yet that he would not grant this request, forasmuch as he had determined the contrary, Ezek. 14:14.
24:15:3: The dogs, birds, and beasts should devour them that were slain.
24:15:4: Not that the people was punished for the king’s sin only, but for their own sins also, because they consented to his wickedness, 2 Kings 21:9.
The word signifieth to run to and fro for fear, and unquietness of conscience, as did Cain.
24:15:6: That is, I will not call back my plagues or spare thee any more.
24:15:8: Because I had slain their husbands.
24:15:9: She was destroyed in the midst of her prosperity.
She that had many, lost all her children.
24:15:10: Which is an occasion of contention and hatred.

By these are the Prophet’s words, complaining of the obstinacy of the people and that he was reserved to so wicked a time: wherein also he showeth what is the condition of God’s ministers, to wit, to have all the world against them, though they give none occasion.
24:15:11: In this perplexity the Lord comforted me, and said that my last days should be quiet: and by the enemy he meaneth here, Nebuzaradan the captain of Nebuchadnezzar, who gave Jeremiah the choice either to remain in his country, or to go whither he would: or by the enemy he meaneth the Jews, which should afterward know Jeremiah’s fidelity, and therefore favor him.
24:15:12: As for the people, though they seemed strong as iron, yet should they not be able to resist the hard iron of Babylon, but should be led captives.
24:15:15: He speaketh not this for desire of revengeance, but wishing that God would deliver his Church of them whom he knew to be hardened and incorrigible.
24:15:16: I received them with a great joy, as he that is famished, eateth meat.
24:15:17: I had nothing a do with the wicked contemners of thy word, but lamented bitterly for thy plagues: showing what the faithful should do when they see tokens of God’s anger.
24:15:18: And hast not assisted me according to the promise? wherein appeareth that in the Saints of God is imperfection of faith, which through impatience is ofttimes assailed, as Jer. 20:7.
24:15:19: Conform not thyself to their wickedness, but let them follow thy godly example.
If thou forget these carnal considerations, and faithfully execute thy charge.
That is, seek to win the good from the bad.
To wit, as my mouth hath pronounced, Jer. 1:18, and as here followeth, verse 20.
24:15:20: I will learn thee with an invincible strength and constancy, so that all the powers of the world shall not overcome thee.
24:16:2: Meaning, that the affliction should be so horrible in Jerusalem, that wife and children should but increase his sorrow.
24:16:5: Signifying, that the affliction should be so great, that one should not have leisure to comfort another.
24:16:6: That is, should not rent their clothes in sign of mourning.
24:16:7: For in these great extremities all consolation and comfort shall be in vain.
24:16:10: Because the wicked are always rebellious, and dissemble their own sins, and murmur against God’s judgments, as though he had no just cause to punish them, he showeth him what to answer.
24:16:15: Signifying, the benefit of their deliverance out of Babylon should be so great, that it should abolish the remembrance of their deliverance from Egypt: but he hath here chiefly respect to the spiritual deliverance under Christ.
24:16:16: By the fishers and hunters are meant the Babylonians and Chaldeans, who should destroy them in such sort, that if they escaped the one, the other should take them.
24:16:18: That is, their sons and daughters, which they offered to Molech.
24:16:19: He wondereth at the great mercy of God in this deliverance, which shall not only extend to the Jews, but also to the Gentiles.
Our fathers were most vile idolaters, therefore it cometh only of God’s mercy, that he performeth his promise, and hath not utterly cast us off.
24:16:21: They shall once again feel my power and mercy for their deliverance, that they may learn to worship me.
24:17:1: The remembrance of their contempt of God cannot pass, albeit for a time he defer the punishment, for it shall be manifest to men and Angels.
Instead of the Law of God, they have written idolatry and all abominations in their heart.
Your sins appear in all the altars that you have erected to idols.
24:17:2: Some read, So that their children remember their altars, that is, follow their fathers’ wickedness.
24:17:3: Zion that was my mountain, shall now be left as a waste field.
24:17:4: Because thou wouldest not give the land rest, at such times, days, and years as I appointed, thou shalt hereafter be carried away, and it shall rest for lack of laborers.
24:17:5: The Jews were given to worldly policies, and thought to make themselves strong by the friendship of the Egyptians, Isa. 31:3, and strangers, and in the mean season did not depend on God, and therefore he denounceth God’s plagues against them, showing that they prefer corruptible man to God, which is immortal, Isa. 2:22; Jer. 48:6, 7.
24:17:9: Because the wicked have ever some excuse to defend their doings, he showeth that their own lewd imaginations deceive them, and bring them to these inconveniences: but God will examine their deeds by the malice of their hearts, 1 Sam. 16:7; 1 Chron. 28:9; Ps. 7:10; Jer. 11:20 and 20:12; Rev. 2:13.
24:17:11: As the Partridge by calling gathered others which forsake her, when they see that she is not their dam: so the covetous man is forsaken of his riches, because he cometh by them falsely.
24:17:12: Showing that the godly ought to glory in nothing, but in God, who doth exalt his, and hath left a sign of his favor in his Temple.
24:17:13: Their names shall not be registered in the book of life.
24:17:14: He desireth God to preserve him that he fall not into tentation, considering the great contempt of God’s word, and the multitude that fall from God.
24:17:15: The wicked say that my prophecy shall not come to pass, because thou deferrest the time of thy vengeance.
24:17:16: I am assured of my vocation, and therefore know that the thing which thou speakest by me, shall come to pass, and that I speak not of any worldly affection.
24:17:17: Howsoever the wicked deal rigorously with me, yet let me find comfort in thee.
24:17:19: Whereas thy doctrine may be best understood both of high and low.
24:17:21: By naming the Sabbath day, he comprehendeth the thing that is thereby signified: for if they transgressed in the ceremony, they must needs be culpable of the rest, read Exod. 20:8, and by the breaking of this one commandment, he maketh them transgressors of the whole law, forasmuch as the first and second table are contained herein.
24:18:4: As the potter hath power over the clay to make what pot he will, or to break them, when he hath made them: so have I power over you to do with you as seemeth good to me, Isa. 45:9; Rom. 9:20, 21.
24:18:8: When the Scripture attributeth repentance unto God, it is not that he doeth contrary to that which he hath ordained in his secret counsel: but when he threateneth, it is a calling to repentance, and when he giveth man grace to repent, the threatening (which ever containeth a condition in it) taketh no place: and this the scripture calleth repentance in God, because it so appeareth to man’s judgment.
24:18:12: As men that had no remorse, but were altogether bent to rebellion and to their own self-will.
24:18:14: As no man that hath thirst refuseth fresh conduit waters which he hath at home, to go and seek waters abroad to quench his thirst: so they ought not to seek for help and succor at strangers, and leave God which was present with them.
24:18:15: That is, the way of truth which God had taught by his law, read Jer. 6:16.
24:18:17: I will show mine anger and not my favor toward them.
24:18:18: Let us slander him, and accuse him: for we shall be believed.

This argument the wicked have ever used against the servants of God. The Church cannot err: we are the Church, and therefore whosoever speaketh against us, they ought to die, 1 Kings 22:24; Jer. 7:4 and 20:2; Mal. 2:4, and thus the false Church persecuteth the true Church, which standeth not in outward pomp, and in multitude, but is known by the graces of the holy Ghost.
24:18:21: Seeing the obstinate malice of the adversaries, which grew daily more and more, the Prophet being moved with God’s Spirit, without any carnal affection prayeth for their destruction, because he knew that it should tend to God’s glory, and profit of his Church.
24:19:3: By Kings here and in other places are meant counselors and governors of the people: which he calleth the ancients, verse 1.
24:19:5: Whereby is declared, that whatsoever is not commanded by God’s word touching his service, is against his word.
24:19:11: This visible sign was to confirm them touching the assurance of this plague, which the Lord threatened by his prophet.
24:19:13: He noteth the great rage of the idolaters, which left no place free from their abominations, insomuch as they polluted their own houses therewith, as we see yet among the Papists.
24:20:2: Thus we see that the thing which neither the King, nor the princes, nor the people durst enterprise against the Prophet of God, this Priest as a chief instrument of Satan first attempted, read Jer. 18:18.
24:20:6: Which have suffered themselves to be abused by thy false prophecies.
24:20:7: Herein appeareth the impatience, which oftentimes overcometh the servants of God, when they see not their labors to profit, and also feel their own weakness, read Jer. 15:18.
Thou didst thrust me forth to this work against my will.
24:20:8: He showeth that he did his office in that he reproved the people of their vices, and threatened them with God’s judgments: but because he was derided and persecuted for this, he was discouraged, and thought to have ceased to preach, save that God’s Spirit did force him thereunto.
24:20:10: Thus the enemies conferred together to know what they had heard him say, that they might accuse him thereof, read Isa. 29:21.
24:20:11: Here he showeth how his faith did strive against tentation, and sought to the Lord for strength.
24:20:14: How the children of God are overcome in this battle of the flesh and the Spirit, and into what inconveniences they fall till God raise them up again: read Job 3:1 and Jer. 15:10.
24:20:16: Alluding to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Gen. 19:25.
24:20:17: Meaning, that the fruit thereof might never come to profit.
24:21:2: Not that the King was touched with repentance of his sins, and so sought to God, as did Hezekiah, when he sent to Isaiah, 2 Kings 19:1; Isa. 37:2, but because the Prophet might pray unto God to take this present plague away, as Pharaoh sought unto Moses, Exod. 9:28.
24:21:4: To wit, from your enemies to destroy yourselves.
24:21:9: As a thing recovered from extreme danger, Jer. 37:2, 39:18 and 45:5.
24:21:13: Meaning, Jerusalem which was built part on the hill, and part in the valley, and was compassed about with mountains.
24:21:14: That is, in the houses thereof, which stood as thick as trees in the forest.
24:22:3: This was his ordinary manner of preaching before the Kings, from Josiah unto Zedekiah, which was about forty years.
24:22:5: Showing that there is none greater than he is, Heb. 6:13, and that he will most certainly perform his oath.
24:22:6: He compareth Jerusalem to Gilead, which was beyond Jordan, and the beauty of Judea to Lebanon.
24:22:7: Thy buildings made of Cedar trees.
The Hebrew word signifieth to sanctify, because the Lord doth dedicate to his use and purpose such as he prepareth to execute his work, Isa. 13:3; Jer. 6:4 and 12:3.
24:22:8: As they that wonder at a thing which they thought would never have come so to pass, Deut. 29:24; 1 Kings 9:8.
24:22:10: Signifying, that they should lose their king: for Jehoiachin went forth to meet Nebuchadnezzar and yielded himself, and was carried into Babylon, 2 Kings 24:12.
24:22:11: Whom some think to be Jehoiachin, and that Josiah was his grandfather: but as seemeth, this was Jehoiakim, as verse 18.
24:22:15: Meaning, Josiah, who was not given to ambition and superfluity, but was content with mediocrity, and did only delight in setting forth God’s glory, and to do justice to all.
24:22:18: For everyone shall have enough to lament for himself.
24:22:19: Not honorably among his fathers, but as carrions are cast in a hole, because their stink should not infect, read 2 Kings 24:9. Josephus Antiquities 10:8, writeth that the enemy slew him in the city and commanded him to be cast before the walls unburied, see Jer. 36:30.
24:22:20: For this was the way out of India to Assyria, whereby is meant that all help should fail: for the Chaldeans have subdued both them and the Egyptians.
To call to the Assyrians for help.
24:22:22: Both thy governors and they that should help thee, shall vanish away as wind.
24:22:23: Thou that art built of the fair Cedar trees of Lebanon.
24:22:24: Who was called Jehoiachin, or Jeconiah, whom he calleth here Coniah in contempt, who thought his kingdom could never depart from him, because he came of the stock of David, and therefore for the promise sake could not be taken from his house: but he abused God’s promise, and therefore was justly deprived of the kingdom.
24:22:29: He showeth that all posterities shall be witnesses of his just plague, as though it were registered for perpetual memory.
24:22:30: Not that he had no children (for after that he begat Shealtiel in the captivity, Matt. 1:12) but that none should reign after him as King.
24:23:1: Meaning, the princes, governors and false prophets, as Ezek. 34:2.
For the which I have especial care, and have prepared good pastures for them.
24:23:2: Whose charge is to feed the flock, but they eat the fruit thereof, Ezek. 34:3.
24:23:3: Thus the Prophets ever used to mix the promises with the threatenings, lest the godly should be too much beaten down, and therefore he showeth how God will gather his Church after this dispersion.
24:23:5: This prophecy is of the restitution of the Church in the time of Jesus Christ, who is the true branch, read Isa. 11:1 and 45:8; Jer. 35:15; Dan. 9:24.
24:23:9: Meaning, the false prophets which deceive the people: wherein appeareth his great love toward his nation, read Jer. 14:13.
24:23:10: They run headlong to wickedness, and seek vain help.
24:23:11: My Temple is full of their idolatry and superstitions.
24:23:14: They which should have profited by my rods against Samaria, are become worse than they.
Though to the world they seem holy fathers, yet I detest them as I did these abominable cities.
24:23:16: Which they have invented of their own brain.
24:23:18: Thus they did deride Jeremiah, as though the word of God were not revealed unto him: so also spake Zedekiah to Micaiah, 1 Kings 22:24.
24:23:20: Both that God hath sent me, and that my words shall be true.
24:23:22: He showeth the difference between the true Prophets and the false, between the hireling and the true minister.
24:23:23: Do I not see your falsehood, however you cloak it, and wheresoever you commit it?
24:23:25: I have a prophecy revealed unto me, as Num. 12:6.
24:23:26: Hebrew, Is it in the heart of the Prophets?
24:23:27: He showeth that Satan raiseth up false prophets to bring the people from God.
24:23:28: Meaning, that it is not sufficient for God’s ministers to abstain from lies, and to speak the word of God: but that there be judgment in alleging it, and that it may appear to be applied to the same purpose that it was spoken, Ezek. 3:27; 1 Cor. 2:13 and 4:2; 2 Tim. 2:25; 2 Pet. 4:10, 11.
Let the false prophet declare that it is his own fantasy, and not slander my word as though it were a cloak to cover his lies.
24:23:30: Which set forth in my Name that which I have not commanded.
24:23:33: The Prophets called their threatenings God’s burden, which the sinners were not able to sustain, therefore the wicked in deriding the word, would ask of the Prophets, what was the burden, as though they would say, You seek nothing else, but to lay burdens on our shoulders: and thus they rejected the word of God, as a grievous burden.
24:23:34: Because this word was brought to contempt and derision, he will teach them another manner of speech, and will cause this word burden to cease, and teach them to ask with reverence, What saith the Lord?
24:23:36: The thing which they mock and contemn, shall come upon them.
24:24:1: The good figs signified them that were gone into captivity, and so saved their life, as Jer. 21:8, and the naughty figs them that remained, which were yet subject to the sword, famine and pestilence.
24:24:5: Whereby he approveth the yielding of Jeconiah and his company, because they obeyed the Prophet, who exhorted them thereunto.
24:24:7: Which declareth that man of himself can know nothing, till God give the heart and understanding.
24:25:1: That is, in the third year accomplished and in the beginning of the fourth: for though Nebuchadnezzar began to reign in the end of the third year of Jehoiakim’s reign, yet that year is not here counted, because it was almost expired, Dan. 1:1.
24:25:3: Which was the fifth year and the ninth month of Jehoiakim’s reign.
That is, I have spared no diligence or labor, Jer. 7:13.
24:25:5: He showeth that the Prophets, wholly with one consent did labor to pull the people from those vices, which then reigned, to wit, from idolatry, and the vain confidence of men: for under these two all others were contained, 2 Kings 17:13; Jer. 18:11 and 35:15; Jonah 3:8.
24:25:9: So the wicked and Satan himself are God’s servants, because he maketh them to serve him by constraint, and turneth that which they do of malice, to his honor and glory.
As the Philistines, Ammonites, Egyptians and others.
The Chaldeans and all their power.
24:25:10: Meaning, that bread and all things that should serve unto their feasts, should be taken away.
24:25:12: For seeing the judgment began at his own house, the enemies must needs be punished most grievously, Ezek. 9:6, 1 Pet. 4:17.
This revelation was for the confirmation of his prophecy, because he told them of the time that they should enter and remain in captivity, 2 Chron. 36:22; Ezra 1:1; Jer. 29:10; Dan. 9:2.
24:25:14: That is, of the Babylonians, as Jer. 27:7.
24:25:15: Signifying, the extreme affliction, that God had appointed for everyone, as Ps. 75:8; Isa. 51:17, and this cup, which the wicked drink, is more bitter than that which he giveth to his children, for he measureth the one by mercy, and the other by justice.
24:25:18: For now it beginneth and shall so continue till it be accomplished.
24:25:20: Which were cities of the Philistines.
24:25:21: Edom is here taken for the whole country, and Uz for a part thereof.
24:25:22: As Greece, Italy and the rest of those countries.
24:25:23: These were people of Arabia which came of Dedan the son of Abraham and Keturah.
24:25:24: For there were two countries so named, the one called plentiful, and the other barren, or desert.
24:25:26: That is, of Babylon, as Jer. 51:41.
24:25:33: They which are slain at the Lord’s appointment.
24:25:34: Ye that are chief rulers, and governors.
24:25:35: It shall not help them to seek to flee.
24:26:2: That is, in that place of the Temple whereunto the people resort out of all Judah to sacrifice.
To the intent that they should pretend no ignorance, as Acts 20:27.
24:26:6: So that when they would curse any, they shall say, God do to thee as to Jerusalem.
24:26:9: Because of God’s promises to the Temple, Ps. 132:14, that he would forever remain there, the hypocrites thought this Temple could never perish, and therefore thought it blasphemy to speak against it, Matt. 26:61; Acts 6:13, not considering that this was meant of the Church, where God will remain forever.
24:26:10: So called, because it was repaired by Jotham, 2 Kings 15:35.
24:26:11: Hebrew, judgments of death belongeth to this man.
24:26:12: He both showeth the cause of his doings plainly, and also threateneth them that they should nothing avail, though they should put him to death, but heap greater vengeance upon their heads.
24:26:18: That is, of the House of the Lord, to wit, Zion, and these examples the godly alleged to deliver Jeremiah out of the Priests’ hands, whose rage else would not have been satisfied but by his death.
24:26:19: So that the city was not destroyed, but by miracle was delivered out of the hands of Sennacherib.
24:26:22: Here is declared the fury of tyrants, who cannot abide to hear God’s word declared, but persecute the ministers thereof, and yet in the end they prevail nothing but provoke God’s judgments so much the more.
24:26:23: As in the first Hezekiah’s example is to be followed, so in this other Jehoiakim’s act is to be abhorred: for God’s plague did light on him, and his household.
24:26:24: Which declareth that nothing could have appeased their fury, if God had not moved this noble man to stand valiantly in his defense.
24:27:1: As touching the disposition of these prophecies, they that gathered them into a book, did not altogether observe the order of times, but did set some afore, which should be after, and contrary wise, which if the reader mark well it shall avoid many doubts, and make the reading much more easy.
24:27:2: By such signs the Prophets used sometimes to confirm their prophecies which notwithstanding they could not do of themselves, but in as much as they had a revelation for the same, Isa. 20:2, and therefore the false Prophets to get more credit, did use also such visible signs, but they had no revelation, 1 Kings 22:12.
24:27:7: They shall bring him and his kingdom in subjection, as Jer. 25:14.
Meaning, Evil-Merodach, and his son Belshazzar.
24:27:16: Which were taken when Jeconiah was led captive into Babel.
24:27:18: For it was not only the Prophet’s office to show the word of God, but also to pray for the sins of the people, Gen. 20:7, which these could not do because they had no express word: for God had pronounced the contrary.
24:27:22: That is, for the space of seventy years till I have caused the Medes and Persians to overcome the Chaldeans.
24:28:1: After that the land hast rested, as Lev. 25:2.
This was a city in Benjamin belonging to the sons of Aaron, Josh. 21:17.
When Jeremiah began to bear these bonds and yokes.
24:28:5: He was so esteemed though he was a false prophet.
24:28:6: That is, I would wish the same for God’s honor, and wealth of my people, but he hath appointed the contrary.
24:28:8: Meaning, that the Prophets that did either denounce war or peace, were tried either true or false by the success of their prophecies, albeit God maketh to come to pass sometimes that which the false prophet speaketh to try the faith of his, Deut. 13:3.
24:28:10: This declareth the impudence of the wicked hirelings, which have no zeal to the truth, but are led with ambition to get the favor of men, and therefore cannot abide any that might discredit them but burst forth into rages and contrary to their own conscience, pass not what lies they report or how wickedly they do, so that they may maintain their estimation.
24:28:14: Signifying, that all should be his, as Dan. 2:38.
That is, a hard and cruel servitude.
